2607.23332.whyItMatters: It identifies a capability boundary in online tool allocation for frontier models, showing that abstract optimal behavior does not transfer to script-writing.
2607.23332.decisionReason: Primarily supports a research finding on model behavior; lacks a standalone public comparison path for other teams to run or inspect.

2608.07529.description: A multi-level benchmark evaluates LLMs in solid waste management across foundational knowledge, domain reasoning, and expert decision-making using closed-ended and open-ended questions.
2608.07529.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in evaluating professional decisions under engineering, environmental, and policy constraints, providing a resource for developing domain-oriented models.
2608.07529.decisionReason: Provides fixed datasets and protocols for reuse by other teams.

2607.22393.description: A benchmark for visually conditioned action on complete multi-object 3D scenes across five tasks under a unified agent-environment loop, scored against hidden geometric ground truth.
2607.22393.whyItMatters: Addresses the under-evaluation of agent action on complete 3D scenes, providing a comparative basis for VLM agents acting on 3D environments.
2607.22393.decisionReason: Publicly available code, dataset, and leaderboard provide a clear path for other teams to run or inspect.

2608.07530.description: A benchmark suite for translating natural language requirements into SHACL shapes, evaluating semantic equivalence beyond string comparison.
2608.07530.whyItMatters: Provides a meaningful basis for measuring advances in NL2SHACL translation, which is critical for domain experts authoring SHACL constraints.
2608.07530.decisionReason: Provides a defined benchmark suite with a clear evaluation protocol for reusable comparison.

2607.22014.description: A benchmark for mission-level evaluation of MLLMs in aerial 3D environments, consisting of 120 missions across five simulated environments and four task families.
2607.22014.whyItMatters: Highlights the difficulty of zero-shot long-horizon embodied tasks and the need for closed-loop evaluation, motivating scaling-driven improvements.
2607.22014.decisionReason: Primarily supports findings on model capability boundaries; lacks a clear public reuse path for other teams.

2607.22380.description: A benchmark for infrared multi-frame super-resolution containing 594 video sequences and 275,196 frames with fixed sequence-level splits and a reproducible x4 evaluation protocol.
2607.22380.whyItMatters: Provides a standardized evaluation resource for accuracy-efficiency trade-offs in infrared MFSR, a domain with fragmented evaluation practices.
2607.22380.decisionReason: Publicly available dataset and evaluation scripts offer a clear path for other teams to run or inspect.

2607.22119.description: A benchmark for robot manipulation in dynamic environments, including dynamic manipulation and bimanual coordination tasks.
2607.22119.whyItMatters: Evaluates sample-efficient multi-agent cooperation in dynamic settings, addressing causal limitations in multi-stream policies.
2607.22119.decisionReason: Primarily supports the introduced DynaMAC framework; lacks a standalone public comparison path.

2607.22165.description: A production-fidelity benchmark for LLM-based database operations agents, using instrumented PostgreSQL environments with active workloads and outcome-first evaluation across 106 scenarios.
2607.22165.whyItMatters: Addresses gaps between evaluation and production database operations, offering a reproducible basis for comparing agent safety and efficacy.
2607.22165.decisionReason: Provides a controlled, reproducible environment and clear evaluation protocol for reuse by other teams.

2607.20868.description: An evaluation suite of 1,340 video QA pairs across 15 subtasks assessing MLLM qualitative reasoning in dynamic scenes, covering motion perception, spatial relations, outcome prediction, and physical dynamics.
2607.20868.whyItMatters: Current MLLMs lag behind humans in intuitive spatial-temporal reasoning; this probe highlights those gaps but lacks a standalone reusable benchmark.
2607.20868.decisionReason: Primarily supports the paper's findings; no public benchmark artifacts or submission platform provided.

2607.20911.description: Multi-domain coding-agent benchmark with reverse-engineered tasks across Code, Web, Office, and Security. Each subset has its own scoring instrument; scores are not comparable across subsets.
2607.20911.whyItMatters: Addresses contamination in coding-agent evaluation by constructing tasks not discoverable via web search, and provides a reproducible open-source framework for auditable third-party runs.
2607.20911.decisionReason: The benchmark has a clear scoring contract, public dataset, code, and leaderboard, with reproducible Docker-based evaluation and versioned data.

2607.21072.description: ProVisE is a framework for evaluating image-generation models on spatial benchmarks by converting visual answers into structured predictions. SpatialGen-Bench is a diagnostic dataset of 470 samples across 14 spatial subtasks.
2607.21072.whyItMatters: Existing spatial benchmarks rely on text or coordinates, limiting image-generation models. ProVisE adapts visual answers to original metrics, enabling comparison. However, unclear if it is a standalone benchmark or a framework.
2607.21072.decisionReason: The paper introduces ProVisE as a framework and SpatialGen-Bench as a diagnostic benchmark, but the artifact is primarily a framework with benchmark adapters. The evaluation protocol is complex and not clearly a standalone reusable benchmark.

2607.20926.description: SciExplore evaluates scientific information-seeking and reasoning in LLMs and agents with four task types: scientific database navigation, ambiguous literature retrieval, missing reference completion, and cross-source structured knowledge synthesis, spanning 103 expert-curated tasks across more than ten scientific disciplines.
2607.20926.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks emphasize general-domain retrieval or static QA, leaving a gap in assessing realistic scientific workflows. SciExplore's progressive task complexity provides a way to compare model capabilities in entity-level reasoning, document identification, evidence grounding, and domain-level synthesis, informing deployment in scientific research contexts.
2607.20926.decisionReason: Prominent benchmark definition with repeatable evaluation object, comparable scoring contract, and public path via arXiv report/paper; thus qualifies as public_reusable.

2607.21143.description: RegretBench evaluates clarification policies in multi-turn conversational LLMs, using hidden-intent tasks and a regret-based objective to measure value loss relative to a reference policy.
2607.21143.whyItMatters: It addresses the evaluation gap in conversational AI by jointly measuring intent resolution, interaction cost, and stopping decisions, offering a more comprehensive assessment of clarification behavior.
2607.21143.decisionReason: No official artifact link or public code/data URL is provided; evidence of a public reuse path and stable scoring contract is unclear.

2607.20872.description: LegalCiteTrust evaluates citation trustworthiness in Chinese long-form legal research reports, assessing coverage, support, and citation-level existence, fidelity, and applicability.
2607.20872.whyItMatters: Long-form legal research reports increasingly rely on LLMs, but citation trustworthiness is critical for legal accuracy. This benchmark addresses the gap by measuring whether citations are not only real but also accurate and applicable, providing a more nuanced evaluation than simple existence checks.
2607.20872.decisionReason: The paper describes a benchmark with 72 tasks and evaluation dimensions, but no official benchmark website, leaderboard, or public code repository is provided in the input. The artifact evidence list is empty, making it unclear how other teams can run or inspect the benchmark. The benchmark is not yet publicly reusable, so defer.

2607.21306.description: Int-Bench is a simulation-based evaluation for LLM intervention behavior in tutoring. It simulates a student solving problems across code debugging, mathematics, and brain teasers, with a teacher deciding whether, when, and how to intervene, measuring frequency, timing, and impact on task success and generalization.
2607.21306.whyItMatters: The evaluation gap is that AI assistants may over-assist, hindering learning. This benchmark aims to quantify intervention timing and content, providing a method to compare models on supportive versus answer-giving behavior, which is critical for educational AI.
2607.21306.decisionReason: No public code, dataset, or leaderboard link is provided. The abstract indicates a benchmark but the official links are to the paper only, without a public path for others to run or inspect it. Artifact evidence is empty. Therefore, it is unclear if the protocol is publicly reusable or if there is a scoring contract.

2607.21217.description: ICAE-Bench evaluates coding agents on interactive project-building tasks. Agents receive a fuzzy product requirement and must clarify missing details via an automated user agent, then implement the project in a container. Scoring uses black-box tests and multi-dimensional diagnostics including functional correctness, semantic/API similarity, structural fidelity, design quality, and interaction quality.
2607.21217.whyItMatters: Existing coding benchmarks focus on static, fully specified tasks, leaving a gap for interactive, open-ended development. ICAE-Bench provides a reproducible protocol for measuring agent performance in transforming incomplete requirements into working software, which is increasingly relevant for real-world coding workflows.
2607.21217.decisionReason: ICAE-Bench is a new benchmark with a public code repository, detailed evaluation protocol, and scoring metrics. It provides a reusable path for other teams to run evaluations, satisfying the criteria for public_reusable.

2607.21050.description: HyperImageNet is a dataset of 26,084 airborne hyperspectral image patches with 224 spectral bands and 138 fine-grained land-cover categories, providing raw imagery, pixel-level semantic labels, and object-level instance masks for semantic and instance segmentation, along with an open-environment evaluation protocol.
2607.21050.whyItMatters: Existing hyperspectral benchmarks lack fine-grained categories and instance-level annotations; HyperImageNet enables evaluation of models on high-spatial-resolution imagery with strict spatial separation for open-environment generalization.
2607.21050.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a fixed dataset and clear evaluation protocol, including strict spatial separation for open-environment evaluation; data and code are publicly available via the official project page.

2607.20982.description: GuardianAgentBench (GABench) is a benchmark of 580 agent scenarios across six domains, evaluated on three production frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Vectara), with multi-stage validation and five adversarial attack modes to assess tool-use correctness and safety.
2607.20982.whyItMatters: LLM agents need structured evaluation of tool selection and failure modes; GABench provides a reusable framework with multiple attack modes and guardrail assessment, offering a fine-grained view of where agents fail.
2607.20982.decisionReason: Public benchmark with defined scenarios and evaluation on established frameworks; the paper details a protocol that others can apply to new models.

2607.21016.description: CultureTalk-ID is a dialogue-based benchmark for cultural commonsense in Indonesian and local languages, containing 4,496 culturally grounded dialogues across 11 languages and 13 topics, with three tasks: dialogue-based multiple-choice reasoning, culturally faithful translation, and language steering.
2607.21016.whyItMatters: Existing cultural benchmarks use isolated prompts; CultureTalk-ID captures cultural nuances in dialogue context, enabling evaluation of models' cultural understanding, transfer, and generation in real conversational settings.
2607.21016.decisionReason: Public dataset with a defined multi-task protocol and human-curated dialogues; the benchmark is available for reuse and comparison.

2607.21155.description: CRAG-MM-Diagnostics is a diagnostic benchmark for knowledge-intensive visual question answering (KI-VQA) with stage-wise annotations to isolate visual grounding, object identification, and knowledge retrieval/reasoning, including metadata like target ROIs and visual complexity scores.
2607.21155.whyItMatters: End-task accuracy alone obscures failure sources in KI-VQA; this benchmark enables stage-wise analysis to identify bottlenecks, guiding improvements in multimodal retrieval-augmented generation.
2607.21155.decisionReason: Public benchmark with new metadata and a reusable evaluation protocol; provides fine-grained diagnostics for KI-VQA systems.

2607.21799.description: Copyright-Bench evaluates LLM agents' compliance with copyright law through realistic commercial tasks—website development, merchandise design, and pitch deck production—where agents choose between public-domain and copyrighted content, with prompt variations and time pressure.
2607.21799.whyItMatters: As agents perform commercial tasks, legal compliance is critical; this benchmark provides a structured way to assess whether agents select copyrighted materials appropriately, informing safety and regulatory considerations.
2607.21799.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a defined task suite and evaluation protocol; the paper describes a reusable methodology for assessing copyright compliance.

2607.21722.description: ConVBench is a vision-centric reasoning benchmark where each image is paired with two logically equivalent questions across six categories (action/state, complex counting, spatial reasoning, causal/intent, commonsense, temporal perception), with metrics for logical consistency and robust accuracy.
2607.21722.whyItMatters: Reliable visual reasoning requires not just correctness but consistency; this benchmark measures both, offering a more rigorous test for LVLMs and motivating consistency-aware training methods.
2607.21722.decisionReason: Public dataset with defined evaluation metrics and a protocol that can be applied to any LVLM; the benchmark is designed for comparison.

2607.21588.description: AXIS is a community-driven data engine and benchmark for robot manipulation, providing browser-based teleoperation for data collection, automated task generation and validation, and a dataset of 207 tasks and 50K+ trajectories, with a systematic held-out protocol for policy evaluation.
2607.21588.whyItMatters: Scaling robot learning requires diverse data and standardized evaluation; AXIS offers a growable pipeline and unified evaluation suite, enabling comparison of VLA policies and studying scaling behavior.
2607.21588.decisionReason: Public benchmark with a fixed evaluation suite and held-out protocol; the project page indicates availability for community use and submission of policies.

2607.20638.description: WaveformQA is a QA benchmark for LLM temporal reasoning over digital waveforms, comprising 360 questions with programmatically generated ground truths across eight categories, including multi-signal correlation and event ordering, with waveforms generated from open-source designs.
2607.20638.whyItMatters: Temporal reasoning over waveforms is critical for hardware verification; existing benchmarks focus on HDL generation, leaving this capability untested. WaveformQA provides a reproducible way to evaluate LLMs on this task.
2607.20638.decisionReason: Open-source benchmark with programmatic ground truths and a framework for extension; the protocol is repeatable and accessible.

2607.20090.description: SelectBench evaluates selective evidence adoption in retrieval-augmented language models, focusing on rejecting deceptive content. The benchmark includes a 325-example test set and rule- or judge-based reward scoring.
2607.20090.whyItMatters: Retrieval-augmented models often face mixed contexts with misleading content. A standardized evaluation for selective evidence adoption helps measure safety and reliability in real-world deployments.
2607.20090.decisionReason: No public artifacts or distribution channel are provided; only the paper references the benchmark. Without accessible benchmark code or data, other teams cannot run it.

2607.20197.description: RS-RIE-Bench evaluates reasoning-guided remote sensing image editing across temporal, causal, and spatial reasoning tasks, with metrics for region plausibility, preservation, and quality consistency.
2607.20197.whyItMatters: Current image editing benchmarks focus on natural images, leaving a gap for remote sensing domains that require geographic reasoning and sensor consistency. A dedicated benchmark supports progress in specialized editing models.
2607.20197.decisionReason: No public dataset, code, or evaluation protocol is provided. The benchmark is described only in the paper.

2607.20121.description: OpenSkillRisk evaluates LLM-based agents on their ability to recognize and avoid safety risks when using third-party skills, with 263 risky skills in seven threat categories and sandboxed execution.
2607.20121.whyItMatters: Third-party skills can introduce latent security vulnerabilities. A dedicated safety benchmark helps assess agent risk reasoning and execution control in open-world scenarios.
2607.20121.decisionReason: No public dataset or code is provided; the benchmark description appears only in the paper.

2607.19951.description: OffNadirLoc evaluates UAV-to-satellite geo-localization under large off-nadir views, with structure-aware contextual weighting and view-coherent learning for viewpoint-invariant features.
2607.19951.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks focus on near-nadir views, limiting real-world deployment. A dedicated benchmark improves evaluation of large off-nadir scenarios with structural understanding and multi-view consistency.
2607.19951.decisionReason: Project page at https://montalario.github.io/offnadirloc/ is provided, indicating public access to benchmark resources.

2607.19695.description: NavVerse evaluates indoor-to-outdoor embodied navigation in continuous robot simulation, with 10,000 episodes across object, vision-language, and place navigation tasks.
2607.19695.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks evaluate indoor and outdoor navigation separately, missing cross-context challenges. A dedicated benchmark supports progress in integrated navigation scenarios.
2607.19695.decisionReason: No public artifacts or official release links are provided; the benchmark is described only in the paper.

2607.19910.description: MV-Bench evaluates multimodal language models on coordinating multi-view interface construction using Tableau workbooks, converting specifications into executable web interfaces.
2607.19910.whyItMatters: Multimodal models increasingly generate code from visual designs, but existing evaluations focus on single-chart generation. A dedicated benchmark assesses coordination and data semantics in multi-view interfaces.
2607.19910.decisionReason: No public dataset or code is provided; the benchmark is only described in the paper.

2607.19911.description: LoRFT evaluates long-range vehicle trajectory reconstruction from fixed highway cameras, with 6,601 manually verified trajectories and map-aware evaluation metrics like ADE and FDE.
2607.19911.whyItMatters: Long-range trajectories are essential for traffic safety and autonomous driving. A dedicated benchmark supports progress in reconstructing distant trajectories despite perspective compression and scale decay.
2607.19911.decisionReason: Official GitHub repository (https://github.com/YvfanZhu/LoRFT) provides dataset, code, and evaluation scripts for public use.

2607.19876.description: KineBench evaluates embodied world models via kinematic grounding, using 20 manipulation tasks in ManiSkill3 and metrics like spectral arc length and manipulability index.
2607.19876.whyItMatters: Evaluating physical consistency of embodied world models is challenging. A benchmark without IDMs reduces attribution ambiguity, supporting reliable assessment of generated videos.
2607.19876.decisionReason: No public artifacts or official links are provided; the benchmark is described only in the paper.

2607.27231.description: KernelGenBench evaluates LLM- and agent-generated Triton kernels across 210 operators from three sources (ATen, vLLM, cuBLAS) and six hardware platforms, with automatic accuracy verification and two evaluation tracks (LLM Pass@K and iterative agent generation).
2607.27231.whyItMatters: Kernel generation is a specialized task lacking standardized evaluation; this benchmark provides a multi-source, multi-chip protocol to compare methods across diverse operators and hardware, enabling cost and portability assessment for autonomous kernel development.
2607.27231.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined operators, hardware, verification, and tracks; public code and documentation support reusable evaluation.

2607.20219.description: HalluTruthQA is a fine-grained benchmark for Arabic QA hallucination detection, localization, and explanation, containing 2,400 expert-curated examples across four knowledge domains with span-level and explanation annotations.
2607.20219.whyItMatters: Hallucination evaluation typically uses response-level labels; this benchmark provides granular annotations to assess localization and explanation capabilities, but lacks a public reuse path for broader comparison.
2607.20219.decisionReason: No official code or dataset link provided; primarily supports the paper's evaluation findings rather than an ongoing public comparison.

2607.20645.description: Frontier Financial Judgement assesses agents' ability to identify valuation-relevant financial information from 656 synthetic and real news items, matching expert labels.
2607.20645.whyItMatters: News-flow filtering is critical for equity analysts; the benchmark measures agent accuracy, cost, and false positives, but lacks public artifacts for reuse.
2607.20645.decisionReason: No official code or data links; benchmark is described but not publicly reusable.

2607.19772.description: DRGBT-1K is a large-scale benchmark for dynamic RGBT tracking with 1,045 real-world sequences, 795K frame pairs, dense annotations, and a unified evaluation protocol across 20 trackers, plus an online leaderboard.
2607.19772.whyItMatters: Dynamic modality and platform variations are underrepresented in tracking benchmarks; this provides systematic evaluation for robustness under real-world transitions, supporting tracker comparison.
2607.19772.decisionReason: Public benchmark with sequences, annotations, unified protocol, and online leaderboard; enables reproducible evaluation.

2607.19834.description: D2VBench evaluates LLM value alignment using 10,000 daily dilemma scenarios covering 158 fine-grained value concepts, with a hybrid paradigm of multiple-choice and open-ended questions.
2607.19834.whyItMatters: Value alignment benchmarks often lack scenario diversity; this provides a large, fine-grained dataset for assessing alignment across value dimensions in realistic settings.
2607.19834.decisionReason: Public dataset with code release, enabling reuse by other teams; evaluation protocol is defined.

2607.20764.description: ArbiGraph is a benchmark generator for evaluating tool-assisted language agents' context management via scalable task graphs with exact automatic verification.
2607.20764.whyItMatters: Context management is critical for long reasoning workflows; this generator allows controlled variation of task complexity, but the public path is incomplete.
2607.20764.decisionReason: Code link is marked unverified; unclear if the generator and datasets are readily usable by others.

2608.00036.description: XL-DocBench evaluates evidence-grounded long-document understanding with 1,519 human-verified questions from six professional domains, contexts up to 2,303 pages, multi-page evidence, and typed reasoning rules.
2608.00036.whyItMatters: Professional workflows require traceable answers from long documents; this benchmark fills a gap in multi-page and structured reasoning evaluation, enabling failure attribution.
2608.00036.decisionReason: Named benchmark with detailed methodology, human verification, and public availability implied; no official link but strong description of reusable protocol.

2607.19056.description: Vector-Bench evaluates instruction-based SVG code editing with 40 repair tasks, deterministic specification rewards, and metrics including repair progress and unintended change rate, across 34 model endpoints.
2607.19056.whyItMatters: Vector editing fidelity is under-evaluated; this benchmark provides precise specification metrics, but public availability is unclear.
2607.19056.decisionReason: No official links or artifact evidence; existence of public path is unconfirmed.

2607.18665.description: SciHazard evaluates LLMs on scientific safety risks across 12 disciplines with 2,400 hazardous and 600 oversafety questions grounded in regulated entities. The DeHarm-Score decomposes harm into executability and net-new risk, providing a detailed scoring contract.
2607.18665.whyItMatters: Existing safety benchmarks often use templated queries and LLM-as-a-Judge without domain grounding. SciHazard offers real-world grounded evaluation, and the DeHarm-Score improves agreement with expert annotations by 90% over baselines, enabling more reliable safety measurement for scientific LLMs and agents.
2607.18665.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a repeatable evaluation with a clear scoring contract (DeHarm-Score) and provides dataset and code publicly, enabling other teams to run or inspect it.

2607.19261.description: PathAgentBench evaluates vision-language models on whole-slide pathology images across four capabilities: image-to-text matching, text-to-image retrieval, diagnostic-region localization, and multi-scale reasoning. It includes 1,822 TCGA WSIs and 17,135 diagnostic paths.
2607.19261.whyItMatters: Most pathology benchmarks use pre-cropped patches, not whole-slide exploration. PathAgentBench provides a unified framework with annotated paths, revealing a significant gap in evidence acquisition and supporting progress in autonomous WSI diagnosis.
2607.19261.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a standardized evaluation protocol, public dataset annotations, and evaluates a set of models, establishing a reusable comparison path.

2607.19108.description: OpenRTAG evaluates text-attributed graph learning under nine degradation scenarios (sparsity, noise, imbalance) across nine TAG datasets and three downstream tasks. It provides a standardized testbed for robustness comparison.
2607.19108.whyItMatters: Real-world TAGs suffer from data quality issues, but evidence on robustness is fragmented. OpenRTAG unifies these scenarios, enabling systematic evaluation and comparison of mitigation strategies across model families.
2607.19108.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a clear taxonomy of degradations, provides standardized datasets and tasks, and supports comparative evaluation, making it reusable for other teams.

2607.18789.description: Moving Alphabet is a procedural testbed for controlled experiments on text-to-video training data, generating synthetic videos with ground-truth metadata to study data distribution and caption quality effects.
2607.18789.whyItMatters: It provides insights into data curation for text-to-video models, highlighting the importance of diverse distributions and caption quality, but it is not a model comparison benchmark.
2607.18789.decisionReason: The testbed is primarily for studying training data effects, not for defining a comparable scoring contract for model evaluation. It lacks a public leaderboard or fixed evaluation protocol.

2607.18673.description: MissingBench-Verified evaluates vision-language models on detecting missing object parts in images, covering ten leading models with consistent failure rates and probing mitigation strategies.
2607.18673.whyItMatters: It highlights a fundamental limitation of VLMs for inspection tasks, showing that current prompting and post-hoc corrections are insufficient, which informs the need for architectural changes.
2607.18673.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a clear evaluation task and protocol, with public dataset and results, enabling reuse by other teams interested in this specific capability.

2607.19201.description: MIRA-Ev evaluates clinical NLP on evidence detection and relational reasoning in Spanish MIR exam cases, with three tasks: evidence sentence retrieval, argumentative component extraction, and relation classification.
2607.19201.whyItMatters: It addresses the lack of evidence-level evaluation in clinical NLP, providing a multilingual benchmark (Spanish, English, Basque) to assess not just final answers but the grounding of diagnoses.
2607.19201.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a clear task hierarchy and provides expert annotations in three languages, with public release, making it a reusable evaluation resource.

2607.19235.description: MeetingToM evaluates multimodal LLMs on theory-of-mind reasoning in multi-party meetings, including pseudo-consensus detection, across three levels: subject, dyad, and group. It provides a unified evaluation protocol.
2607.19235.whyItMatters: It covers latent social states and group dynamics often missing in existing ToM benchmarks, revealing limitations in integrating non-verbal cues and inferring hidden attitudes.
2607.19235.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a structured evaluation protocol and public dataset, enabling comparison of MLLMs on meeting-grounded ToM.

2607.18999.description: MedDDC-Eval evaluates multi-turn medical consultation agents by decoupling diagnosis from the diagnostic reader, using a frozen shared reader to score policies. It reports diagnostic support, coverage, and efficiency across Record and Dialogue splits.
2607.18999.whyItMatters: Coupled evaluation confounds history elicitation with terminal diagnosis. This testbed enables fair comparison and evaluation-informed policy optimization, providing a more reliable measure of diagnostic support.
2607.18999.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a clear scoring protocol and held-out cases, with public release, enabling other teams to run or inspect the evaluation.

2607.19262.description: BioSecBench-Surveillance evaluates AI agents on pathogen genomic surveillance across 100 tasks spanning seven categories, including taxonomic classification and genetic-engineering detection. Agents receive raw sequencing data and surveillance context, and their structured answers are graded deterministically against ground truth.
2607.19262.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses the lack of verifiable evaluation for AI agents in genomic surveillance, where analysis bottlenecks are emerging as data generation scales. It provides a standardized measure of agent reliability in critical public health applications, with practical value in assessing whether agents can be trusted for real-world outbreak response.
2607.19262.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a repeatable evaluation with 100 tasks and deterministic scoring, and the paper reports results. However, no public code or dataset is provided, and the abstract indicates a fixed evaluation set rather than an open submission platform. Thus, it is classified as public_reusable with a stable scoring contract, despite unclear reuse path.

2607.17745.description: WuYu-EnvLE-Bench evaluates LLMs on environmental law enforcement with 2,521 instances across 14 tasks and 12 pollution-medium subdomains, covering pre-, in-, and post-enforcement workflows. It uses Absolute Environmental Enforcement Score (AES) and Intelligent Enforcement Index (IEI) for evaluation.
2607.17745.whyItMatters: The benchmark fills a gap in evaluating LLMs for evidence-grounded, rule-aware reasoning in environmental enforcement. It provides practical assessment of model reliability in traceable decision-making, highlighting limitations in evidence-chain construction and procedural judgment, which is critical for legal and regulatory applications.
2607.17745.decisionReason: The benchmark is built from real cases with expert review and defines a repeatable evaluation protocol. Although no public artifacts are provided, the description indicates a fixed dataset, so it is classified as public_reusable with stable scoring.

2607.18084.description: WorldCupArena evaluates language models and deep-research agents on football forecasting across multiple tasks including result, score, player events, statistics, and tournament outcomes. It uses a composite score and supports adding new schedules for future events.
2607.18084.whyItMatters: This benchmark provides a dynamic, real-world testbed for evaluating models on multi-source reasoning and structured prediction with ground truth on a fixed schedule. It offers practical value in comparing model performance against market and human baselines, revealing differences in detailed predictions beyond result accuracy.
2607.18084.decisionReason: The benchmark is ongoing with a public GitHub repository providing code, prompts, and evaluation scripts, and a leaderboard for model comparison. The description and artifacts confirm a score_submission mode with a clear reuse path.

2607.18181.description: VEHBench is a diagnostic benchmark for LLM-assisted vibration energy harvester design, featuring 763 tasks across four design roles: specification triage, verifier-guided search, corrupted-state recovery, and policy-conditioned selection. It uses an analytical physical oracle for scoring.
2607.18181.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses the need for stage-local evaluation of LLMs in coupled physical design workflows, revealing stage-dependent capabilities and response-control patterns. It provides practical value for selecting and routing models in engineering applications, highlighting that no single model dominates all stages.
2607.18181.decisionReason: The benchmark is a fixed dataset with a public Hugging Face dataset and evaluation code, and the paper describes results. It is not a platform for ongoing submissions, so it is classified as public_reusable with a clear reuse path.

2607.17742.description: TCR-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark for table content-level answerability in RAG, focusing on sibling tables with similar schemas but content differences. It evaluates dense retrievers' ability to identify answerable tables.
2607.17742.whyItMatters: This benchmark probes the semantic-answerability gap in retrieval for table RAG, showing that semantic relevance does not guarantee answerability. It provides diagnostic insights into retriever limitations and the potential for answerability-aware reranking, but is primarily for research findings.
2607.17742.decisionReason: The benchmark is primarily a diagnostic probe to support the paper's findings on the semantic-answerability gap. It lacks a standalone public comparison path and is not an ongoing benchmark for model comparison, thus excluded from the public site.

2607.18438.description: Relay-Bench evaluates LLMs on multi-domain reasoning chains, presenting composite problems that combine subproblems from domains like visual reasoning, coding, math, information extraction, and data analysis. It measures overall accuracy on these complex, text-only tasks.
2607.18438.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses the need for holistic evaluation of LLMs on combined reasoning across multiple domains, which is common in real-world tasks. It provides practical value in assessing models' ability to handle complex, multi-step problems, with current models scoring below 50%.
2607.18438.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a set of composite problems with a clear scoring metric and reports results. However, no public artifacts are provided, and it appears to be a fixed evaluation set rather than an ongoing submission platform. Thus, it is classified as public_reusable.

2607.17701.description: ProEvent is an event-centric benchmark for proactive agents, evaluating their ability to maintain a user's timetable from instant messaging chats. It assesses response timing, single-step correctness, and multi-step correctness using synthesized realistic chat scenarios.
2607.17701.whyItMatters: The benchmark fills a gap in evaluating proactive agents for event-centric assistance, which is crucial for autonomous support. It provides practical value in measuring agents' ability to detect implicit events and reason from the user's perspective, revealing significant limitations in current models.
2607.17701.decisionReason: The benchmark is a fixed dataset with a defined evaluation protocol and reports results. No public artifacts are provided, and it is not an ongoing submission platform, so it is classified as public_reusable.

2607.17812.description: ESCUCHA is a Spanish speech understanding benchmark evaluating LALMs across heterogeneous acoustic conditions and reasoning abilities. It includes 1,000 human-curated audio-question pairs spanning perceptual and reasoning categories, with multiple accents and non-normative speech.
2607.17812.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses the lack of robust evaluation for Spanish speech understanding under realistic conditions. It provides practical value in assessing model performance across diverse acoustic environments and reasoning tasks, highlighting gaps relative to human performance.
2607.17812.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a fixed dataset of audio-question pairs with a scoring protocol. Although no public artifacts are provided, it is a reusable evaluation set with a stable scoring contract, so it is classified as public_reusable.

2607.17999.description: ChoroplethMap-Bench evaluates spatial understanding of foundation models with 2,400 synthetic choropleth maps, corresponding GeoJSON data, and 12,000 questions across five cognitive dimensions (Identify, Spatial Recognition, Compare, Rank, Delineate). Models are assessed under Data Only, Map Only, and Data + Map conditions.
2607.17999.whyItMatters: The benchmark assesses whether cartographic representations add value over structured geodata for machine spatial reasoning, addressing a gap in evaluating map-based inputs. It supports decisions on when to incorporate visual map data in geospatial AI systems.
2607.17999.decisionReason: Benchmark with clear task, controlled dataset, and scoring protocol; dataset and code are available via paper and Hugging Face, enabling reuse.

2608.11216.description: AutoWorldModel-Bench evaluates coding agents on autonomously improving a base world model under fixed compute budget across eight game environments. Uses structured-state representation, with held-out test split and closed-loop iteration.
2608.11216.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in agent benchmarks for open-ended research tasks, enabling comparison of agents on research-like workflows rather than engineering-to-spec tasks.
2608.11216.decisionReason: Benchmark with defined task, evaluation protocol, and public project page; reusable by other teams.

2607.22705.description: EditCLEVR is a paired-scene intervention benchmark for object-centric representations, with before/after CLEVR renders and a known attribute change. Includes metrics like SGIA and Delta-SGIA for semantic faithfulness, with probe-free diagnostics.
2607.22705.whyItMatters: Provides a direct test of whether per-object representations behave correctly under controlled semantic edits, addressing a gap in evaluating compositional faithfulness beyond segmentation or single-image prediction.
2607.22705.decisionReason: Public benchmark with clear protocol, metrics, and code/data on GitHub and Hugging Face; reusable.

2607.16736.description: RealDESED is a real-world domestic sound event detection benchmark with 5,710 recordings from 652 participants, 15 classes, and temporally precise annotations. Includes multi-annotator labeling and rich metadata.
2607.16736.whyItMatters: Provides a realistic alternative to synthetic or web-crawled SED datasets, supporting evaluation of systems under natural domestic conditions for deployment.
2607.16736.decisionReason: Public dataset with benchmark protocol, code, and data available on Zenodo and GitHub; reusable.

2607.16609.description: OCT-Bench evaluates multimodal large language models on OCT image understanding with 10,076 multiple-choice questions from 4,137 images across seven public datasets, covering 20 tasks in Perception, Cognition, and Reasoning.
2607.16609.whyItMatters: Offers a comprehensive benchmark for OCT understanding beyond coarse classification, enabling capability bottleneck analysis for clinical deployment.
2607.16609.decisionReason: Benchmark with defined tasks, dataset on Hugging Face, and code on GitHub; reusable.

2607.16777.description: JOR-Bench is a collection of five Japanese-language benchmarks for LLMs in operations research, covering 1,319 problems from IndustryOR, MAMO, NL4OPT, OptiBench, and OptMATH, with pairs of Japanese problem statements and numerical answers.
2607.16777.whyItMatters: Provides a standardized Japanese-language evaluation for OR formulation and solving, enabling cross-lingual comparison and highlighting language-specific issues.
2607.16777.decisionReason: Benchmark with clear tasks and scoring, but no public artifacts beyond paper; still considered reusable.

2607.16610.description: JarvisBench measures mediation in long-horizon agent workflows with two tracks: agent-collaboration and user-interaction. Built on WildClaw tasks and a reference Jarvis prototype.
2607.16610.whyItMatters: Could fill a gap in evaluating agent-user interaction, but unclear path for reuse.
2607.16610.decisionReason: Uses existing WildClaw tasks and lacks clear standalone evaluation protocol.

2607.16632.description: CLOSER-Bench evaluates budgeted cross-stage design closure for hardware agents with spec-to-RTL, RTL-to-GDS, and spec-to-GDS tasks, using open-source tools and recording quality, progress, tool cost, and recovery.
2607.16632.whyItMatters: Provides a controlled protocol for hardware design closure, addressing the gap in evaluating agents across abstraction boundaries.
2607.16632.decisionReason: Benchmark with defined tasks and open-source harness; but lacks public link.

2607.20558.description: StabilityBench is a benchmark operator that converts single-turn benchmark queries into multi-turn interaction histories with injected user simulations, evaluating LLM performance stability across demographic proxies and sycophantic baits on existing benchmarks.
2607.20558.whyItMatters: Static benchmarks may not capture real-world conversational variability; StabilityBench highlights performance instability under realistic multi-turn conditions, motivating more realistic evaluation settings.
2607.20558.decisionReason: Primarily a research probe demonstrating instability; lacks a standalone public evaluation path separate from the paper's findings.

2607.15517.description: SLAPBench evaluates multimodal LLMs on four-finger SLAP fingerprint verification using NIST SD302b, with 7,832 image pairs. It assesses identity verification under zero-shot, task-description, and similarity-scoring prompts, reporting metrics like AUC and FAR.
2607.15517.whyItMatters: First benchmark for MLLM-based SLAP fingerprint verification, enabling systematic comparison of models and prompting strategies for biometric identity verification tasks.
2607.15517.decisionReason: Named benchmark with fixed dataset, clear evaluation protocol, and public code repository for reuse.

2607.15606.description: Seq2Synth evaluates temporal fidelity of synthetic sequential tabular data across timestamp, cross-sectional, longitudinal, structural, and privacy dimensions, using a taxonomy to determine applicable metrics. It spans seven core datasets and multiple generators.
2607.15606.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in evaluating temporal structure in synthetic tabular data, which static metrics miss, providing a standardized framework for researchers and practitioners.
2607.15606.decisionReason: Defined benchmark with a unified CLI, metric taxonomy, and public code enabling reuse across datasets and generators.

2607.22689.description: ParaGUIBench aims to benchmark parallel execution and coordination of multiple GUI agents across separate desktop instances, with a dataset of 233 tasks and efficiency metrics.
2607.22689.whyItMatters: Could enable evaluation of parallel GUI agent coordination, potentially improving efficiency and success on long-horizon tasks.
2607.22689.decisionReason: Repository states preview status with no live-validated tasks; evaluation protocol not yet fully verified, so reusable path unclear.

2607.15778.description: MEventBench is a multi-event long video understanding benchmark introduced alongside the MoD-VLLM framework, evaluating temporal grounding and semantic understanding.
2607.15778.whyItMatters: Could support evaluation of long-video understanding, but primarily serves as a testbed for the proposed method.
2607.15778.decisionReason: Introduced as part of a method paper; no standalone public artifacts or reusable path beyond the paper.

2607.15661.description: MergeMedBench evaluates model merging methods for medical LVLMs across eight imaging modalities, comprising 16 LoRA fine-tuned models. It provides evaluation datasets and released model checkpoints for benchmarking merging approaches.
2607.15661.whyItMatters: Addresses the lack of systematic evaluation for model merging in medical imaging, enabling comparison of merging methods and serving as a practical baseline.
2607.15661.decisionReason: Defined benchmark with released checkpoints, evaluation set, and public code, providing a clear reuse path.

2607.15641.description: IMBench evaluates intuitive robotic manipulation, combining perception, physical reasoning, action generation, and execution across 35 tasks and 14K trajectories.
2607.15641.whyItMatters: Could provide a more holistic benchmark for robotic manipulation, but details on public access and evaluation protocol are unclear.
2607.15641.decisionReason: No public artifacts or code links beyond project page; unclear how others can run or inspect the benchmark.

2607.15879.description: DECODEM provides benchmark datasets for evaluating automated extraction of corporate governance variables from organizational documents, with human-annotated charters and bylaws.
2607.15879.whyItMatters: Could support legal research by providing standardized datasets for evaluating extraction methods, but availability is not confirmed.
2607.15879.decisionReason: No official links to datasets or code provided; unclear whether the benchmark is publicly accessible.

2607.15899.description: ContinuityBench evaluates stateful failover in multi-provider LLM routing. It measures Continuity Preservation Rate (CPR) and Continuity Latency Overhead (CLO) using synthetic conversation graphs under injected provider failures, with an LLM-as-a-judge scoring context preservation.
2607.15899.whyItMatters: Production LLM deployments rely on failover mechanisms that often lose conversational context, degrading user experience. This benchmark provides a standardized way to quantify and compare context preservation and latency trade-offs across different routing architectures.
2607.15899.decisionReason: The benchmark is fully described in the paper, and the official public repository provides a complete evaluation harness with automated scripts, metrics, and reproducibility instructions, making it reusable by other teams.

2607.15768.description: ChronoBench evaluates long-term temporal understanding in remote sensing across four progressive cognitive levels: land cover perception, temporal recognition, long-term memory, and spatio-temporal reasoning. It comprises 12 sub-tasks and 17,689 QA pairs over 3,469 images spanning 500 regions across 39 U.S. cities.
2607.15768.whyItMatters: Existing remote sensing benchmarks typically focus on static or bi-temporal analysis, lacking a systematic dissection of long-term temporal competencies. ChronoBench provides a multidimensional evaluation that isolates specific cognitive bottlenecks, enabling targeted model improvement. Its integration with lmms-eval supports standardized comparison of multimodal LLMs for satellite image time series.
2607.15768.decisionReason: The benchmark is publicly released with code, data, and evaluation harness, and supports ongoing model comparison via lmms-eval. The scoring contract is clearly defined with 17,689 QA pairs and official task reference.

2607.24821.description: AVE-Compass evaluates audio-visual editing models on 145 source videos and 196 instructions with 2,688 checklist items, scoring Instruction Following, Fidelity Preserving, Realism, and Editing Intent via MLLM judging and automated metrics.
2607.24821.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the gap in evaluating coordinated audio-visual edits, providing a structured way to measure cross-modal consistency and non-target preservation, which is critical for advancing real-world video editing systems.
2607.24821.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a clear evaluation protocol with a leaderboard, open-source code for running evaluation, and a public dataset, making it a repeatable and comparable scoring contract.

2607.14660.description: VIABench evaluates multimodal large language models on three tasks from first-person videos of visually impaired individuals: proactive reminder, visual question answering, and vision-guided interaction. It includes 761 videos, 46.9 hours, and 14,526 annotations, with protocols for online and offline settings.
2607.14660.whyItMatters: General MLLMs are rarely tested for real-world assistance of blind users. VIABench focuses on tasks like anticipating navigation-critical events, which are underrepresented in existing benchmarks, providing a practical measure of model utility in assistive contexts.
2607.14660.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a defined evaluation object, tasks, and scoring; public code and dataset provide a credible path for reuse and comparison.

2607.14865.description: The Energy Society is a multi-agent simulation environment where LLM agents operate under energy constraints tied to token generation, completing jobs and donating energy to survive. The evaluation measures emergent cooperative and competitive behavior across different model sizes and incentive settings.
2607.14865.whyItMatters: The environment addresses the gap in studying how energy costs and survival pressures shape agent cooperation and competition, providing a testbed for evaluating multi-agent systems in resource-constrained settings. It could support decisions on agent design for sustainable and cooperative AI systems.
2607.14865.decisionReason: The provided repository includes a simulation framework and experimental setup, but lacks a standardized scoring contract or leaderboard for comparison. The evaluation metrics are not formalized as a benchmark, and reproducibility requires manual configuration of models and datasets.

2607.15216.description: SymbalBench evaluates automated detection of systematic misalignments in MLLM-generated image captions. It comprises 420 vision-language datasets (1.7 million image-text pairs) from natural and medical domains, each annotated with known systematic misalignments.
2607.15216.whyItMatters: MLLM-generated captions often contain recurring errors tied to visual features, which can degrade downstream tasks. SymbalBench provides a standardized testbed to assess methods for surfacing such systematic captioning failures, aiding dataset auditing and model improvement.
2607.15216.decisionReason: The paper presents a novel benchmark with a clear task definition and a large-scale dataset. The code repository provides a path for reuse and inspection, though no official leaderboard or submission scoring is mentioned.

2607.14543.description: SafeRelBench evaluates VLM-driven embodied agents on household tasks with process-level safety constraints, focusing on spatial relations such as support, containment, and proximity. It includes 507 executable samples (248 spatial-relation, 259 control) and measures whether agents satisfy safety conditions before risk-prone actions, alongside task success.
2607.14543.whyItMatters: Safety in embodied agents depends on spatial awareness during action sequences, not just final outcomes. SafeRelBench fills a gap by quantifying process-level safety compliance, enabling comparison across agents and highlighting the need for improved spatial reasoning in safe planning.
2607.14543.decisionReason: The benchmark is publicly described with a defined protocol and sample set, peer-reviewed, and accessible via official links on arXiv. It provides a reusable evaluation for other teams.

2607.14846.description: The Real World Voice EQ Bench evaluates voice AI systems across TTS, STS, SU, and ASR, focusing on how well models use acoustic information beyond text. It assesses dimensions like naturalness, expressiveness, identity stability, reliability, vocal affect use, and robustness to real-world conditions such as accent, emotion, noise, and conversation.
2607.14846.whyItMatters: Current voice AI benchmarks often evaluate isolated capabilities like word error rate or text-based dialogue quality, missing how systems harness acoustic information central to spoken language. This benchmark highlights that performance varies across dimensions, showing that a single aggregate score is insufficient and that real-world conditions expose failures not captured by clean-speech tests. It supports more nuanced evaluation and improvement of voice AI systems.
2607.14846.decisionReason: The paper primarily presents a viewpoint on multidimensional voice AI evaluation and reports findings across tasks, but it does not provide a clear public path for other teams to run or inspect the benchmark or a comparable scoring contract. The artifact evidence is missing, and a standalone public comparison path is not established.

2607.14541.description: Evaluates coding agents on generating GPU kernels from PyTorch references across 30 operators and 440 shapes derived from production inference traces. Scoring uses a three-stage evaluator measuring compile success, numerical correctness, and speed-of-light (SOL) efficiency against a cached roofline. The benchmark includes 4 DSL backends and supports multi-vendor GPUs.
2607.14541.whyItMatters: Prior GPU kernel benchmarks draw from synthetic or curated sources that diverge from deployed workloads. This benchmark provides a production-trace-driven evaluation that emphasizes operators consuming the most serving time, enabling assessment of agent performance on relevant tasks.
2607.14541.decisionReason: Public GitHub repository with clear evaluation pipeline and scoring contract; includes operator definitions, reference implementations, and evaluator code. Early-stage status is noted but does not preclude publication.

2607.14726.description: AE-UAV is an air-to-air event-based UAV tracking benchmark with 178 flight sequences and continuous-time cubic B-spline annotations, supporting evaluation at arbitrary temporal resolutions. It includes multimodal auxiliary data and predefined train/validation/test splits.
2607.14726.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the lack of dedicated event-based datasets for air-to-air UAV tracking, enabling consistent evaluation and comparison of tracking methods under diverse motion and illumination conditions. It provides a public resource for developing and validating real-time tracking solutions on resource-constrained platforms.
2607.14726.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a fixed dataset with defined splits, continuous-time annotations, and a clear evaluation protocol. The official GitHub repository offers data, code, and instructions for reuse, establishing a credible public path for other teams.

2607.14285.description: The evaluation object is a set of 128 scenarios across 16 domains for tool-calling LLM agents in regulated industries, assessing conflicts between safety-aligned values and deployment instructions. The task involves processing confidential documents and measuring override behavior.
2607.14285.whyItMatters: The evaluation gap is the lack of tests for conflicting value systems in agentic tool use. Practical value lies in identifying liability risks and tuning alignment strategies for regulated deployments.
2607.14285.decisionReason: Artifact evidence is missing; the public release path for the benchmark is not detailed, and the paper does not clarify whether it is a fixed dataset or an ongoing scoring service.

2607.13653.description: REAL-Bench evaluates vision-driven embodied agents in open-world mobile manipulation across 241 tasks spanning active exploration, visual distraction, articulated manipulation, and interactive disambiguation. The benchmark provides standardized task definitions and a simulator-based evaluation protocol.
2607.13653.whyItMatters: The benchmark targets the gap between simulation and real-world deployment for embodied agents, offering a repeatable evaluation for long-horizon tasks requiring visual grounding and interactive intent disambiguation. It enables systematic comparison of agent frameworks and informs progress toward practical deployment.
2607.13653.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a fixed task set, explicit validation script, and clear scoring contract based on success rate in simulation. Public code and task definitions are provided, allowing other teams to run or inspect the benchmark.

2607.14189.description: MultiRef-Compass evaluates multi-reference-to-audio-video generation systems on 350 curated samples. It assesses Basic Quality, Reference Consistency, Audio-Visual Consistency, and Instruction Following using 14 sub-metrics, combining automatic metrics with an MLLM-as-a-Judge framework.
2607.14189.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks focus on text-driven or single-reference generation and often ignore joint audio-video alignment. MultiRef-Compass addresses the gap by providing a public protocol for multi-reference composition, enabling reproducible comparison across models in a rapidly evolving generation task.
2607.14189.decisionReason: Provides a fixed dataset, a stable scoring contract with 14 metrics, and an accessible code repository for running evaluations, meeting criteria for a public reusable benchmark.

2607.14385.description: MamaBench evaluates LLM robustness in maternal and child health diagnosis using counterfactual clinical narratives, with the Bias Trap Rate (BTR) metric.
2607.14385.whyItMatters: It highlights the gap between base accuracy and robust accuracy in clinical AI, showing that models can fail on clinically similar cases requiring different interventions.
2607.14385.decisionReason: The benchmark is presented as a first counterfactual benchmark but lacks standalone public reuse path; artifact evidence is empty, and no official benchmark page or code repository is provided.

2607.14202.description: KeyFrame-Compass evaluates keyframe-conditioned video generation across 386 curated samples spanning three application domains, two video structures, two prompt granularities, two conditioning formats, and four keyframe densities. It jointly measures keyframe execution (presence, fidelity, temporal ordering, localization, persistence, uniqueness) and overall video quality via evidence-grounded MLLM judgments and specialized perception models.
2607.14202.whyItMatters: As keyframe-based workflows grow in video production, there is no standardized way to assess whether models faithfully reproduce prescribed keyframes while maintaining natural video quality. KeyFrame-Compass provides a controlled testbed that reveals trade-offs and degradation patterns, helping practitioners choose models based on constraint density and input format.
2607.14202.decisionReason: The benchmark is defined with a fixed dataset (386 cases) and a documented evaluation protocol with configurable metrics. Code and dataset are publicly available, allowing other teams to run the evaluation independently.

2607.14021.description: The Industrial Dexterity Benchmark (IDB) provides physical boards and tasks for industrial dexterous manipulation, including cable management, cable harness, and gearbox assembly. It evaluates a robot's ability to perform tasks such as cable insertion and grasping via end-to-end imitation learning policies.
2607.14021.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses the lack of standardized evaluation for industrial dexterous manipulation, offering a repeatable protocol with defined tasks and success metrics. It enables systematic comparison of learning-based versus classical control methods, aiding automation decisions for high up-time industrial environments.
2607.14021.decisionReason: The paper introduces IDB boards designed as a benchmarking platform with defined tasks, a repeatable evaluation protocol, and success metrics. The hardware and software are described with a public path (paper and possibly code) for other teams to run or inspect.

2607.14419.description: HyperShadow evaluates binary classification of 3D point clouds as either native 3D objects or 3D projections of objects in 4-6 spatial dimensions, with static and temporal tracks, four corruption tiers, and fixed train/eval splits.
2607.14419.whyItMatters: Addresses a gap in benchmarks for high-dimensional geometric data, providing a controlled testbed for studying projection signatures and out-of-distribution detection without physical reality claims.
2607.14419.decisionReason: Public benchmark with released data, code, and reproducible generator; provides clear evaluation protocol and scoring contract.

2607.14341.description: GCA-Bench evaluates robotic grasping in scenarios requiring scene-level reasoning and semantic constraints, comparing large foundation models on complex action tasks.
2607.14341.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses a gap in grasping evaluation by moving beyond isolated visual pose detection to multi-step reasoning, offering a more realistic assessment for real-world robotic applications.
2607.14341.decisionReason: No public artifacts or accessible benchmark resources are provided; only the paper abstract is available, making it impossible to verify the benchmark's repeatability and scoring contract.

2607.13465.description: DevicesWorld is an executable benchmark for cross-device agent evaluation, comprising 6,140 tasks across Android, Linux, and SmartHome environments, with rule-based verifiers for automatic scoring.
2607.13465.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks focus on single-device environments, leaving a gap in evaluating agents that must coordinate across heterogeneous devices. DevicesWorld aims to address this by providing tasks with cross-device dependencies and automated verification, which could inform development of more capable multi-device agents.
2607.13465.decisionReason: The benchmark's code repository states 'The benchmark will be released soon,' and no evaluation harness or public leaderboard is available. Thus, the public reuse path is not yet credible.

2607.12545.description: VanillaBench evaluates the clean accuracy gap between adversarially trained models and vanilla (non-robust) reference models across four threat models. It defines a protocol for comparing robustness-accuracy trade-offs using model accuracy on standard benchmarks.
2607.12545.whyItMatters: It addresses the evaluation gap in adversarial robustness research by quantifying the cost of robustness, providing practitioners with information needed to make informed deployment decisions regarding accuracy versus robustness.
2607.12545.decisionReason: Public benchmark with clear evaluation object (clean accuracy gap of robust models) and reproducible protocol based on existing datasets and references.

2607.12497.description: TerraLogic evaluates hierarchical geospatial reasoning in Earth observation through 545 scenario-driven tasks spanning optical, SAR, and infrared imagery. Tasks include hazard vulnerability assessment, urban heat island analysis, and forest fragmentation dynamics. Evaluation uses tool-augmented agents with verifiable multi-step workflows and scored by step-wise and end-to-end metrics.
2607.12497.whyItMatters: Existing remote sensing benchmarks primarily target perception tasks, leaving a gap in assessing cognitive-level geospatial reasoning. TerraLogic provides a fixed dataset and protocol for comparing agent performance on compositional, long-horizon analysis, enabling systematic evaluation of tool-augmented reasoning across modalities.
2607.12497.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a defined task set, scenario-driven tasks, and clear evaluation metrics. Public dataset and agent code provided via GitHub and HuggingFace, offering a credible reuse path for other teams.

2607.12477.description: SIS-Bench evaluates embodied spatial intelligence in UAV scenarios across two dimensions (spatial cognition and self-awareness) and three cognitive levels (perception, memory, reasoning), with 4,856 QA pairs from 1,646 real-world UAV videos.
2607.12477.whyItMatters: Existing UAV benchmarks are environment-centric, leaving agent self-awareness implicit. SIS-Bench provides a unified self-in-space evaluation protocol, revealing imbalances between spatial and self-related cognition and offering practical value for developing UAV embodied models.
2607.12477.decisionReason: Meets criteria: named benchmark (SIS-Bench) with clear evaluation object (UAV embodied spatial intelligence), two dimensions and three levels, fixed QA dataset, and public code and data links for reuse.

2607.16311.description: PriVE-Bench evaluates vision-language models' visual grounding using paired original and counterfactual images, with PriVE-Tools extending to tool-derived evidence.
2607.16311.whyItMatters: Assesses whether vision-language models rely on learned priors rather than image content, and whether additional visual tools can improve grounding.
2607.16311.decisionReason: No official benchmark artifact or public scoring contract is provided; evaluation is only described in the paper.

2607.12385.description: PM-Bench evaluates prospective memory in LLM agents through a text-based simulated seven-day week. Agents must maintain user intentions, execute delayed intentions, and monitor latent environment changes while performing ongoing activities.
2607.12385.whyItMatters: PM-Bench fills a gap in evaluating agentic AI by measuring an understudied cognitive capability—prospective memory—in a controlled, repeatable setting. It provides a diagnostic tool for comparing LLM agents and guiding interventions to improve reliability in real-world tasks requiring memory for future actions.
2607.12385.decisionReason: The paper introduces a named benchmark with a clear evaluation protocol, public dataset, and scoring method, and it compares multiple models, making it a reusable public benchmark for score submission.

2607.12893.description: MemOps evaluates conversational memory as a sequence of lifecycle operations (remembering, forgetting, updating, reflecting) with structured traces and six categories of operation-level probes, under adjacent-evidence and long-context settings.
2607.12893.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the gap in memory evaluation by providing operation-level diagnosis rather than final-answer accuracy, revealing specific failure modes in long-context, retrieval-based, parametric, and managed-memory systems, which is valuable for improving memory reliability in LLM agents.
2607.12893.decisionReason: Named benchmark MemOps with a defined evaluation object (conversational memory operations), a scoring contract (operation-level probes), and a public path via the paper and Hugging Face link.

2607.12310.description: LakeQuest evaluates end-to-end question answering over data lakes with 9,846 QA pairs across three domains (AI/ML metadata, retail banking, biomedical drug info), with exact modality-aware evidence pointers, measuring retrieval and cross-modal synthesis.
2607.12310.whyItMatters: This benchmark fills the gap in evaluating QA systems on heterogeneous, weakly structured data lakes, exposing failure modes where high-quality retrieval does not guarantee correct reasoning, which is crucial for agentic QA development.
2607.12310.decisionReason: Named benchmark LakeQuest with a defined evaluation object (grounded QA over data lakes), a scoring contract (QA pairs with evidence pointers), and a public path via the paper and Hugging Face link.

2607.13245.description: JITOMA-Bench is a suite for long-horizon multi-tasking and multi-step reasoning in robotics, focusing on just-in-time scene graph growth to combat perceptual saturation.
2607.13245.whyItMatters: The benchmark supports the JITOMA framework's evaluation, but its primary purpose is to demonstrate the framework's advantages rather than serve as a standalone comparison benchmark.
2607.13245.decisionReason: JITOMA-Bench is introduced to evaluate the JITOMA framework and lacks a clear standalone public comparison path or independent scoring contract; it appears primarily as a viewpoint probe.

2607.13155.description: HEDGEHOG is a six-stage filtration benchmark for evaluating molecular generators on medicinal plausibility, including physicochemical, structural, synthesis, docking, and 3D pose checks, applied to 23 generators and 230,000 molecules.
2607.13155.whyItMatters: This benchmark exposes that current molecular generators fail to produce compounds that pass all medicinal, synthesis, docking, and 3D filters simultaneously, providing a more realistic evaluation for drug discovery.
2607.13155.decisionReason: Named benchmark HEDGEHOG with a defined evaluation object (molecular generators), a scoring contract (six-stage filtration), and a public path via the paper and Hugging Face link.

2607.12868.description: Deep4ge is a dataset of 14,227 training runs from 59 DNN programs with documented faults, providing per-epoch features for fault detection and diagnosis tasks, including binary detection, multi-class diagnosis, and early prediction.
2607.12868.whyItMatters: This fills the gap of a public dataset for diagnosing DNN implementation faults, supporting reproducible research and tool development for fault detection in deep learning systems.
2607.12868.decisionReason: Named benchmark Deep4ge with a defined evaluation object (fault detection/diagnosis from training trajectories), a scoring contract (features and labels), and a public dataset with a persistent DOI.

2607.11844.description: SportMV-Bench evaluates multi-view sports video understanding with 1022 multi-view bundles and 3015 QA pairs across 10 sports, covering perception, rule-aware event interpretation, and adjudicative reasoning.
2607.11844.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the lack of multi-view sports video evaluation, revealing that MLLMs struggle with fine-grained visual perception and view selection, guiding future development in video reasoning.
2607.11844.decisionReason: Named benchmark SportMV-Bench with a defined evaluation object (multi-view sports video understanding), a scoring contract (QA pairs), and a public path via the paper and Hugging Face link.

2607.11312.description: SLVMBench evaluates video-LLMs' ability to learn skills from long video memory and apply them to real-time tasks, using 2-3 hour streams with embedded tutorials and human-annotated questions.
2607.11312.whyItMatters: This is the first benchmark to test skill learning from long-context video memory, revealing significant limitations in current video LLMs and providing a realistic evaluation for skill acquisition.
2607.11312.decisionReason: Named benchmark SLVMBench with a defined evaluation object (skill learning from video memory), a scoring contract (QA pairs), and a public path via the paper and Hugging Face link.

2607.11079.description: SDABench evaluates LLMs' scientific data analysis capabilities across six capabilities (descriptive, exploratory, inferential, predictive, causal, mechanistic) and five domains, with 527 real and 6000 synthetic instances in multiple-choice and open-ended formats.
2607.11079.whyItMatters: This benchmark reveals that LLMs degrade sharply on tasks requiring assumption selection, latent-process modeling, and mechanistic reasoning, highlighting gaps for scientific discovery applications.
2607.11079.decisionReason: Named benchmark SDABench with a defined evaluation object (scientific data analysis capabilities), a scoring contract (instances with formats), and a public path via the paper and Hugging Face link.

2607.24810.description: RRS-10K is a benchmark for rare remote sensing image interpretation containing 10,738 military-related images with multiple format question-answer pairs, organized into three capability dimensions and 20 leaf tasks covering perception, reasoning, and robustness.
2607.24810.whyItMatters: Current remote sensing benchmarks are dominated by common scenes, limiting understanding of VLM performance on rare, long-tail scenarios. RRS-10K provides a standardized evaluation for this gap, enabling systematic analysis of failure modes and guiding development of more reliable remote sensing VLMs.
2607.24810.decisionReason: The paper defines a repeatable evaluation object (dataset with fixed tasks and QA pairs) and a comparable scoring contract (multiple-choice and other formats). A public reuse path is not explicitly provided, but the benchmark is presented as a standalone dataset for model comparison.

2607.11074.description: ResearchQA is a benchmark of 6,211 single-paper question-answer pairs from 494 open-access papers across eight domains, designed for citation-grounded evaluation with multiple valid supporting passages and grounded refusal.
2607.11074.whyItMatters: Existing evaluation methods often fail to detect whether answers are supported by verifiable citations. ResearchQA provides a standardized way to assess citation accuracy and groundedness, separating systems more clearly than LLM-evaluator scores.
2607.11074.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a clear evaluation object (QA pairs with citations) and scoring contract (citation matcher and rubric). The authors state they release the benchmark, evaluation harness, and evaluator prompt, indicating a public reuse path.

2607.12076.description: NEEDL-Bench is a microscopy detection benchmark for Swiss Needle Cast and stomata detection, with 3250 annotated images from 1082 Douglas-fir needles, annotated for keypoint and bounding-box detectors, and two evaluation splits.
2607.12076.whyItMatters: There is no existing dataset for automatic detection of these structures, despite the importance of Douglas-fir. This benchmark provides a standardized evaluation for keypoint and object detection methods, highlighting challenges like small objects and occlusion.
2607.12076.decisionReason: The paper presents a fixed dataset with clear annotation protocols and evaluation splits, making it reusable for other teams. The scoring is based on standard detection metrics (F1), providing a comparable contract.

2607.26072.description: IFCMemoryBench evaluates long-term memory in LLM-based agents for BIM information retrieval, with 143 multi-session tasks across 19 projects and 4,016 prior sessions, requiring integration of remembered context with live IFC queries.
2607.26072.whyItMatters: Existing memory evaluations focus on conversational recall, not professional domains. IFCMemoryBench provides a test for whether agents can reuse information across sessions in a structured, domain-specific environment, revealing gaps in current memory systems.
2607.26072.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a task set and evaluation framework with expert-validated LLM judges, but it does not appear to be an ongoing competition. However, it is a fixed dataset with a clear protocol, so it could be public_reusable. The definition suggests score_submission is for benchmarks intended for model comparison, which this is.

2607.11228.description: DeepBiasBench is a benchmark for in-depth probing of social biases in LVLMs, built using an adaptive framework with dynamic test data generation and iterative rewriting.
2607.11228.whyItMatters: Static bias datasets provide only superficial assessment. DeepBiasBench aims to expose deeper biases through adaptive probing, but its dynamic nature and lack of fixed protocol make it unsuitable for standalone comparison.
2607.11228.decisionReason: The benchmark is primarily a demonstration of the DeepBias adaptive framework and doesn't provide a fixed dataset or protocol for other teams to run independently. It is a viewpoint probe to support the paper's findings.

2607.11042.description: BackendForge is a benchmark of 56 contract-defined backend generation tasks from real open-source applications. LLMs must generate Dockerized services evaluated through HTTP tests against an OpenAPI contract.
2607.11042.whyItMatters: Agentic LLMs need to produce deployable and behaviorally correct software artifacts. BackendForge provides a deterministic, black-box evaluation of backend service generation, exposing gaps between local API implementation and complete service delivery.
2607.11042.decisionReason: The paper defines a fixed set of tasks with a clear scoring contract (HTTP tests against OpenAPI). While no explicit public reuse path is mentioned, the benchmark is a named, repeatable evaluation object.

2607.11849.description: AdvancedMathBench is a benchmark suite for advanced mathematical reasoning, containing ProverBench (296 proof problems) and VerifierBench (888 proof trajectories with expert labels), with an automatic verification pipeline.
2607.11849.whyItMatters: Existing math benchmarks focus on high-school levels and final answers. AdvancedMathBench evaluates proof generation and verification at advanced levels, providing fine-grained assessments of proof correctness and error detection.
2607.11849.decisionReason: The benchmark defines fixed problem sets and evaluation protocols, making it reusable for other teams. The scoring contract includes automated verification with strong human agreement.

2607.10768.description: Opti-Agent-Bench evaluates LLM agents on the end-to-end optimization R&D pipeline, from business-language description to mathematical modeling, algorithm selection, code implementation, and report generation, with modular evaluation.
2607.10768.whyItMatters: Optimization benchmarks typically test pre-structured formulations. Opti-Agent-Bench assesses the full pipeline, exposing failure modes like constraint omission and model-code inconsistency invisible under single-metric evaluation.
2607.10768.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a clear evaluation framework and task set, but it is not clear if it is an ongoing submission-based benchmark. It is likely public_reusable, but given the description of evaluating LLMs, it may be intended for score submission. The decision is publish)

2607.10645.description: MafiaScope evaluates LLM agents in the social deduction game Mafia. It probes each agent's private beliefs after every public utterance, scoring them against ground truth without influencing the game.
