2607.02825.whyItMatters: It addresses the need for realistic and leakage-aware evaluation of vulnerability detection models, offering multiple split strategies and contamination audits to separate genuinely unseen CVEs from memorized ones.
2607.02825.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a defined task (vulnerability detection), a scoring contract (presumably detection metrics), and public availability via Zenodo and a demonstration video, enabling reusable and ongoing evaluation.

2607.02440.description: EvoPolicyGym evaluates autonomous policy evolution in interactive RL environments. A harness-model agent iteratively edits an executable policy under a fixed interaction budget. The benchmark records trajectories of programs, submissions, feedback, and selection, and scores agents on held-out episodes.
2607.02440.whyItMatters: Existing evaluations often collapse iterative improvement into a final score or confound it with software-engineering progress. EvoPolicyGym isolates the capability to improve policies from bounded feedback, providing trajectory-level diagnostics that distinguish how agents allocate budget and refine policies. This supports comparison of agents on a controlled, reusable protocol.
2607.02440.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a standardized evaluation protocol, a unified interface to interactive environments, and a public code repository with documentation for authoring and running evaluations. It defines a scoring contract with held-out validation and assessment, and offers a public path for other teams to run or inspect it.

2607.02269.description: AnyGroundBench evaluates video grounding in vision-language models across five specialized domains (animal, industry, sports, surgery, public security) with spatio-temporal annotations. It provides training and test splits per domain for zero-shot and in-context learning evaluation.
2607.02269.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap between existing benchmark evaluations on general daily-life videos and real-world specialized applications. Provides a structured domain-adaptation protocol to assess model adaptability in specialized fields, enabling comparative evaluation of VLMs in practical scenarios.
2607.02269.decisionReason: Public benchmark with released code and data splits, clear evaluation scripts, and stated scoring contract. Offers a repeatable evaluation protocol for domain-adaptive video grounding.

2607.01647.description: Evaluates LLM-based data agents on realistic data science workflows across 15 domains, with fine-grained ground-truth labels and skill-level scoring.
2607.01647.whyItMatters: Addresses the lack of comprehensive benchmarks for automating data science workflows, providing fine-grained skill-level insights to guide agent development and selection.
2607.01647.decisionReason: Benchmark with public code, datasets, and a leaderboard; provides a clear evaluation protocol and submission path.

2607.00664.description: YOMI-Bench evaluates kanji reading and phonological understanding in LLMs for Japanese through four tasks. It is used in a study assessing multilingual and Japanese-specific models.
2607.00664.whyItMatters: There is no standalone public comparison path or shared artifact; the benchmark primarily supports the paper's finding that LLMs struggle with kanji reading.
2607.00664.decisionReason: The benchmark is introduced in a paper with no public artifact evidence or official links beyond the paper itself; it serves as a viewpoint probe for the study's findings.

2607.01388.description: RusFinChain is a Russian-language benchmark for verifiable chain-of-thought reasoning in finance, comprising 5,280 parameterized examples generated from executable Python templates across 17 domains and 172 topics. Each example includes a gold-standard reasoning chain with intermediate numeric values for automatic verification, and the dataset, code, and evaluation framework are publicly released.
2607.01388.whyItMatters: Most financial reasoning benchmarks lack step-level supervision and are English-only; RusFinChain addresses this gap by providing a contamination-free, verifiable CoT benchmark for Russian, enabling automatic assessment of intermediate reasoning steps. It introduces improved metrics that better correlate with final-answer correctness, supporting more diagnostic evaluation of financial LLMs for the Russian-speaking community.
2607.01388.decisionReason: This is a new benchmark with a defined evaluation object (financial CoT reasoning), a scoring contract (step-level verification with gold chains, plus fuzzy/soft metrics), and a clear public path (dataset, code, evaluation framework released). It is not a viewpoint probe, does not merely use existing benchmarks, and is not a non-benchmark.

2607.00436.description: PHREEQC-MCQ-200 evaluates tool-augmented agents on 200 multiple-choice questions derived from 21 validated PHREEQC scenarios. Agents must construct simulator inputs, execute PHREEQC, inspect structured outputs, and commit to final answers. Scoring is based on exact match of selected answer.
2607.00436.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the lack of standardized evaluation for tool-augmented agents in scientific simulation, measuring not only accuracy but also item-level retention, output-access sensitivity, and trajectory failures. It provides a diagnostic lens on when tool access improves or degrades performance, informing design of reliable scientific agents.
2607.00436.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a repeatable evaluation object (200 MCQ from validated PHREEQC scenarios) with a clear scoring contract (accuracy on multiple-choice answers) and a credible public path via the paper and Hugging Face. It is intended for public reuse as a diagnostic benchmark for scientific agent evaluation, not solely for a single paper's viewpoint.

2607.01360.description: PAIR-Bench evaluates code improvement by transforming incorrect programs into more correct ones through feedback-guided refinement. It uses progressive hinting with failure-region and hint-depth controls to measure repair of targeted failures, generalization beyond the hint, preservation of correct behavior, and required assistance.
2607.01360.whyItMatters: Traditional binary pass/fail metrics miss partial progress and refinement trajectories. PAIR-Bench provides finer-grained, progressive metrics to assess how LLMs improve code through feedback, offering practical value for developing and selecting models for code improvement tasks.
2607.01360.decisionReason: The abstract describes a named benchmark (PAIR-Bench) with a repeatable evaluation protocol (progressive hinting) and scoring metrics. While no explicit public code/data URL is provided in the input, the benchmark is presented as a standalone evaluation object. Given the description and the presence of an arXiv paper, it meets the criteria for a public reusable benchmark.

2607.00724.description: MSQA evaluates 1,064 natively sourced questions across 11 language groups, five cultural dimensions, and three difficulty tiers, testing cultural knowledge in a multilingual context.
2607.00724.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap in measuring cultural alignment separately from language ability, revealing that models often fail to achieve cultural competence despite multilingual fluency.
2607.00724.decisionReason: Provides a fixed set of questions with defined scoring, usable by other teams.

2607.00464.description: MolSafeEval evaluates safety risks in AI-generated molecules across four task types, using structured knowledge graphs and LLM-based reasoning to detect unsafe features.
2607.00464.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in molecular generation benchmarks by focusing on safety risks, providing standardized datasets and protocols for safer molecular design.
2607.00464.decisionReason: Defines a repeatable evaluation with standardized datasets and protocols.

2607.01117.description: MoHallBench evaluates motion hallucination in video LLMs with 11,306 video clips and 40,493 QA pairs, covering three hallucination sources and multiple choice settings.
2607.01117.whyItMatters: Targets a specific video understanding failure mode, offering metrics to reduce affirmation bias and revealing gaps in action recognition vs. hallucination resistance.
2607.01117.decisionReason: Provides a fixed dataset and protocol usable by other teams.

2607.00491.description: MindEdit-Bench evaluates counterfactual spatial reasoning in VLMs with 1,003 multiple-choice questions from private indoor scenes, covering six task types.
2607.00491.whyItMatters: Tests whether VLMs can reason about hypothetical object manipulations, a capability not covered by existing benchmarks, with human-verified answers.
2607.00491.decisionReason: Dataset and evaluation protocol are publicly available on HuggingFace.

2607.01071.description: MemSyco-Bench evaluates memory-induced sycophancy in agent systems across five tasks, measuring how memory influences decision-making and personalization.
2607.01071.whyItMatters: Addresses a gap in memory benchmarks by focusing on downstream reasoning effects, offering a leaderboard and standardized evaluation code.
2607.01071.decisionReason: Provides a leaderboard and code for submission, with clear evaluation pipeline.

2607.01086.description: LongVQUBench evaluates long-term video quality understanding with 1200+ videos and 1500 questions across three levels of perceptual reasoning complexity.
2607.01086.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in video quality benchmarks by focusing on temporal continuity and cumulative degradation, with hierarchical evaluation levels for systematic assessment.
2607.01086.decisionReason: Defines a fixed dataset and protocol for evaluating video quality understanding.

2607.00700.description: LLVM-Bench evaluates LLMs on resolving LLVM compiler issues with 423 real-world tasks, using an automated evaluation platform.
2607.00700.whyItMatters: Provides a large-scale benchmark for system-level compiler issue resolution, addressing a gap in LLM evaluation for complex software engineering tasks.
2607.00700.decisionReason: Offers a fixed dataset and evaluation platform for reuse.

2607.01431.description: IsoSci evaluates reasoning vs. knowledge retrieval in LLMs using isomorphic cross-domain problem pairs, enabling controlled attribution of reasoning gains.
2607.01431.whyItMatters: Provides a method to separate reasoning ability from knowledge, challenging assumptions about chain-of-thought and guiding model evaluation.
2607.01431.decisionReason: Dataset is publicly available and protocol is defined.

2607.00547.description: EgoGapBench evaluates egocentric action selection in multi-agent scenes, isolating the ability to choose actions from the agent's perspective when other agents are present. The benchmark includes training and test splits with human performance as reference.
2607.00547.whyItMatters: Existing egocentric benchmarks conflate first-person view processing with perspective-taking, making it hard to isolate perspective understanding. EgoGapBench fills this gap by providing a controlled evaluation for a capability that is crucial for embodied AI and human-robot interaction, showing that state-of-the-art models fail at this task.
2607.00547.decisionReason: Public benchmark with available code, defined evaluation protocol, and scoring metrics (accuracy). Provides a reusable path for other teams to run.

2607.19380.description: CruiseBench evaluates remaining useful life prediction for aircraft engines using a fixed cruise-stage protocol derived from N-CMAPSS. It provides a reproducible sub-benchmark with datasets and baseline results for LSTM, GRU, TCN, and TSMixer models under specific settings.
2607.19380.whyItMatters: RUL prediction is critical for maintenance planning, but existing benchmarks like N-CMAPSS lack evaluation control due to full-flight records. CruiseBench offers a controlled, reproducible setting for fair comparison of RUL models, reducing variability from stage and preprocessing choices.
2607.19380.decisionReason: Proposes a benchmark with a fixed protocol, but no code or dataset link is provided in the input, and the public reuse path is unclear. Defer due to lack of artifact evidence.

2607.00711.description: ClarifyCodeBench evaluates LLMs on clarifying ambiguous requirements for code generation through interactive dialogues. It includes manual annotations of ambiguity types, clarification questions, and ground-truth answers, with metrics for interaction quality.
2607.00711.whyItMatters: Code generation in practice involves underspecified requirements, but existing benchmarks assume perfect prompts. ClarifyCodeBench addresses this by measuring a critical yet underexplored capability, revealing that strong code generation does not imply effective requirement clarification.
2607.00711.decisionReason: Defines a novel benchmark with clear scoring metrics, but no public artifacts or code are provided in the input, making the public reuse path unclear. Defer due to insufficient evidence.

2607.02606.description: ChainSWE evaluates coding agents on sequential, dependent bug fixes within a shared codebase. It includes 304 issues across 54 Python projects, forming chronological chains, and measures performance drop as chain length increases.
2607.02606.whyItMatters: Real-world software maintenance involves streams of related defects, but existing benchmarks evaluate one bug at a time. ChainSWE fills this gap by benchmarking agents on continuous workflows, revealing significant performance degradation on longer chains.
2607.02606.decisionReason: Proposes a benchmark with defined protocol, but no public artifacts or code are provided in the input, and reuse path is unclear. Defer due to insufficient evidence.

2607.00726.description: AV-SyncBench evaluates audio-visual synchronization by separating temporal and semantic consistency. It contains 3,269 videos and 38,390 samples across 10 scenarios and 5 tasks, with data filtered and verified for on-screen sound sources.
2607.00726.whyItMatters: Existing AV feature extraction evaluations are coupled, preventing independent assessment of temporal and semantic alignment. AV-SyncBench provides a decoupled benchmark to quantify feature quality for alignment and downstream tasks.
2607.00726.decisionReason: Public benchmark with available dataset and code via project website, clear evaluation tasks, and defined metrics. Provides a reusable path for other teams.

2607.01152.description: AGC-Bench evaluates artificial general creativity across 78 datasets covering brainstorming, problem solving, STEM, narrative, figurative language, and humor. It uses an agentic harness and a public leaderboard with an open-weight judge model.
2607.01152.whyItMatters: Creativity is a key aspect of intelligence often overlooked in AI evaluation. AGC-Bench provides a comprehensive, standardized measurement of AI creativity, revealing distinct strengths and weaknesses across models and a single creativity factor analogous to general intelligence.
2607.01152.decisionReason: Public benchmark with a leaderboard, code, and human data. Provides a reusable path for evaluation and submission.

2606.31672.description: WorldRoamBench evaluates interactive world models on long-horizon stability across action, vision, physics, and memory dimensions. It includes 600+ test cases in various scenes and views with continuous interaction.
2606.31672.whyItMatters: Interactive world models need stable, physically grounded, and memory-faithful behavior, but existing benchmarks ignore these aspects. WorldRoamBench provides a comprehensive evaluation revealing that no current model reliably satisfies all dimensions.
2606.31672.decisionReason: Proposes a benchmark with clear protocol, but no public artifacts or code are provided in the input, and reuse path is unclear. Defer due to insufficient evidence.

2607.00107.description: VULBENCH-CPP evaluates the safety of AI-generated C++ code using multi-tier verification including functional testing, static analysis, dynamic analysis, and bounded model checking. It includes 8,918 programs from three LLMs and human authors.
2607.00107.whyItMatters: Security of AI-generated code is critical, but evaluations often rely on a single method. VULBENCH-CPP provides a comprehensive multi-tier benchmark that reveals AI code is more prone to runtime violations and that no single verification tier is sufficient.
2607.00107.decisionReason: Introduces a benchmark with a defined protocol, but no public artifacts or code are provided in the input, and reuse path is unclear. Defer due to insufficient evidence.

2606.31875.description: SENSE-VAD is a synthetic video anomaly detection dataset for autonomous driving, generated with CARLA and Unreal Engine. It includes socially complex anomalies across five categories with per-frame binary labels, plus real-world videos for sim-to-real transfer.
2606.31875.whyItMatters: Addresses the evaluation gap for socially complex anomalies in autonomous driving, which are not captured by motion-based detectors. Provides a controlled benchmark to test current video anomaly detection models.
2606.31875.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear task, annotated dataset, and generation code publicly available. Offers a standalone evaluation path for other teams.

2606.31689.description: ScratchWorld is an offline diagnostic benchmark for world models, using Scratch projects as executable worlds. It evaluates next-state prediction, long-horizon tracking, causal attribution, and counterfactual prediction with replay-verified transitions.
2606.31689.whyItMatters: Provides a new evaluation paradigm for world models that avoids confounds like overlap with persistent state. Enables direct comparison of model capabilities on executable consequences.
2606.31689.decisionReason: Publicly available benchmark with clear evaluation protocol and metrics. Offers a reusable diagnostic tool for the research community.

2606.32034.description: QVal is a training-free testbed for evaluating dense supervision signals for long-horizon LLM agents. It measures Q-alignment of scores from methods across four environments and seven families, without requiring training runs.
2606.32034.whyItMatters: Fills the gap of direct, comparable evaluation of dense supervision methods, which is currently expensive and confounded. Enables early-stage assessment before training.
2606.32034.decisionReason: Publicly available code and benchmark with a clear evaluation methodology and extensible design. Provides a reusable testbed for the community.

2606.31154.description: PPT-Eval is a benchmark of 120 PowerPoint tasks across 12 files for computer-use agents. It covers content creation and editing, with rubric-based evaluation that awards partial credit and provides natural language feedback.
2606.31154.whyItMatters: Provides a realistic, multimodal testbed for computer-use agents. The rubric-based scoring captures partial progress and correlates with human judgment, enabling nuanced comparison.
2606.31154.decisionReason: Named benchmark with public project page and defined evaluation protocol. Offers a reusable evaluation framework for PowerPoint tasks.

2606.31966.description: MECoBench is a multimodal embodied cooperation benchmark with an evaluation platform. It spans real-world tasks, two cooperation structures, and three collaboration modes, with code and dataset publicly available.
2606.31966.whyItMatters: Systematically evaluates collaboration among multimodal embodied agents, a relatively unexplored area. Provides a testbed for understanding collaboration mechanisms and limits.
2606.31966.decisionReason: Named benchmark with public code and dataset, including evaluation scripts and simulator. Offers a reusable platform for embodied collaboration research.

2606.31745.description: JL1-CC&QA is a multi-task benchmark extending JL1-CD with change captioning and question answering. It includes 17,021 captions and 20,060 QA pairs over 5,000 bi-temporal image pairs from Jilin-1 satellite.
2606.31745.whyItMatters: Bridges the semantic gap in remote sensing change detection by providing captions and QA alongside binary masks. Enables multi-task understanding of surface changes.
2606.31745.decisionReason: Publicly available dataset with clear annotation structure and the JL1-CD base dataset. Offers reusable resources for change understanding.

2606.31767.description: JETO-Bench is a benchmark of 660 execution time improvement patches (ETIPs) in Java, with 91 manually verified. It is built using JETO-Mine, a configurable tool that mines ETIPs from GitHub repositories and statistically validates improvements.
2606.31767.whyItMatters: Provides a reproducible benchmark for performance bug fixing in Java, an area lacking benchmarks. Enables evaluation of patch generation and test generation tools.
2606.31767.decisionReason: Publicly available benchmark and tool, with Docker images and evaluation harness. Offers a reusable pipeline for creating benchmarks.

2606.31308.description: InterFLOPBench is a benchmark of 90 C kernels and 1,130 test samples for evaluating LLMs on floating-point error classification across six categories: cancellation, comparison, division by zero, overflow, underflow, and NaN.
2606.31308.whyItMatters: Provides a targeted evaluation for LLM capabilities in static floating-point error detection, a niche but important area. Enables comparison across models and error types.
2606.31308.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined task and evaluation metric (F1-score). The dataset is described but no official link provided; however, the benchmark is presented as a standalone dataset.

2606.31179.description: Evaluates AI agents on 54 realistic healthcare tasks across 7 categories, including medical imaging, EHR analysis, and clinical trial matching. Agents operate in terminal environments with task-specific verifiers and a final task success rate.
2606.31179.whyItMatters: Provides a standardized, realistic evaluation for agentic healthcare AI, revealing performance gaps across task types and informing model selection for clinical applications.
2606.31179.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a fixed suite of tasks with verifiers, public code repository, and scoring protocol. Official arXiv paper and GitHub link confirm it as a reusable benchmark for agent evaluation.

2606.31522.description: Evaluates the longitudinal stability of behavioral mandates in LLM-based financial agents using a synthetic market simulation that decouples observable price from hidden fundamental value, scoring mandate adherence across calm, crash, and bubble market regimes.
2606.31522.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap in evaluating long-horizon behavioral consistency of autonomous financial agents, providing a falsifiable method to measure mandate salience decay and informing deployment decisions for mandate-aware re-grounding strategies.
2606.31522.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a fixed simulation protocol and scoring contract; public artifact via arXiv paper; reusable by other teams.

2607.00218.description: EgoSafetyBench is a diagnostic egocentric video benchmark of 1,200 robot-view scenarios to evaluate vision-language models as runtime safety guards. It assesses situational awareness across routine, suspicious, obvious, and contextual hazards, and visual-channel robustness against misleading in-scene text.
2607.00218.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the practical need for safety guards that distinguish genuine hazards from superficially alarming but benign actions, and highlights the vulnerability to misleading signage, which can inform safer deployment of embodied VLMs in real-world settings.
2607.00218.decisionReason: The benchmark primarily supports the paper's findings on VLM deficiencies; no public code, dataset, or leaderboard is provided, and the protocol is not standardized for external comparison.

2606.31174.description: ClawArena-Team evaluates a single text-only LLM's ability to manage a fixed, locally served pool of subagents (LLM, VLM, omni) across 41 multi-turn, multimodal, multi-directory scenarios with 258 evaluation rounds and 72 staged updates. Scoring is execution-based via shell commands, producing a Subagent-Management Score (SMS) that multiplies task correctness by a least-privilege and modality-routing factor, without LLM judges.
2606.31174.whyItMatters: Existing agent benchmarks measure a policy's own task-solving or emergent behavior of fixed multi-agent systems, but not the leadership capability of a single model orchestrating subagents. ClawArena-Team fills this gap by isolating management skill from raw capability, supporting decisions on model selection for delegation-heavy workflows and revealing cost-quality trade-offs.
2606.31174.decisionReason: The paper provides a repeatable evaluation object (41 scenarios, 258 rounds) with a stable scoring contract (execution-based SMS no LLM judge) and a public reuse path via open-source code, dataset, and leaderboard with submission channel.

2606.31435.description: CDR-Bench is a benchmark of 3,462 tasks for evaluating large language models on faithful execution of compositional, order-sensitive data refinement recipes across four domains and 29 operators, with deterministic reference outputs for exact evaluation.
2606.31435.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks leave unclear whether LLMs can directly execute multi-step, order-sensitive data refinement tasks; this benchmark provides a reusable, deterministic evaluation protocol to assess procedural faithfulness in compositional text processing.
2606.31435.decisionReason: The CDR-Bench benchmark defines a clear evaluation object (data refinement recipes) and scoring contract (exact match against deterministic reference outputs), and provides a public dataset on ArXiv. It is a standalone public benchmark, not a viewpoint probe or uses-existing.

2606.29957.description: SWE-Together evaluates coding agents in multi-turn interactive user sessions reconstructed from real user-agent interactions. It comprises 109 repository-level tasks with a reactive LLM-based user simulator, measuring final repository correctness and the number of corrective feedback turns.
2606.29957.whyItMatters: Existing coding-agent benchmarks often evaluate static, single-turn tasks, missing the interactive nature of real coding assistance. SWE-Together provides a reproducible protocol for assessing agents as collaborators, capturing both task success and user effort, offering practical value for comparing agents in realistic settings.
2606.29957.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a defined set of tasks, a user simulator, and a scoring contract for correctness and user correction, with public code and dataset allowing other teams to run or inspect it.

2606.30573.description: SWE-Interact evaluates coding agents on multi-turn, interactive software engineering tasks where a simulated user provides vague instructions, reveals requirements progressively, and gives feedback. The benchmark comprises 75 tasks and measures agents' ability to discover user intent, adapt to evolving requirements, and build on prior work.
2606.30573.whyItMatters: Existing SWE benchmarks focus on single-turn autonomous implementation, but real developer workflows are interactive. SWE-Interact fills the gap by measuring performance on long-horizon, user-driven tasks, showing that strong single-turn performance does not reliably transfer. This provides a more realistic evaluation axis for coding agents and guides development of models that can collaborate effectively with users.
2606.30573.decisionReason: The benchmark is a named, repeatable evaluation object with a scoring contract (rubric-based grading) and a public repository providing task data, run configs, and instructions for running the tasks. It is a fixed dataset/protocol usable by other teams for comparison.

2606.29955.description: SpreadsheetBench 2 evaluates spreadsheet agents on end-to-end business workflows across generation, debugging, and visualization tasks. It includes 321 tasks from authentic business data, with multi-sheet workbooks requiring cross-sheet reasoning. The benchmark provides a unified multi-turn agent scaffold and evaluation scripts for reproducibility.
2606.29955.whyItMatters: Existing spreadsheet benchmarks focus on isolated operations, failing to capture real-world workflow complexity. SpreadsheetBench 2 addresses this gap by assessing agents on tasks that require multi-step coordination, cross-sheet reasoning, and deliverable-level outcomes. It provides a challenging testbed for improving reliable spreadsheet automation, with current models achieving only 34.89% overall accuracy.
2606.29955.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a public dataset, code, and evaluation scripts (GitHub link), enabling other teams to run or inspect it. It has a clear scoring contract and is intended for model comparison, satisfying the criteria for public_reusable.

2606.30201.description: SHOVIR evaluates vision shortcut learning in radiology report generation by extending MIMIC-CXR and PadChest-GR with per-box CheXpert labels. It defines image-level and disease-level occlusion experiments that compare model predictions on clean images against localized perturbations to isolate direct and contextual shortcut failures at the disease-class level.
2606.30201.whyItMatters: Standard RRG metrics miss whether diagnostic statements are grounded in actual image evidence, allowing models to exploit dataset priors. SHOVIR provides a protocol to assess spatial grounding, revealing that high report quality can coexist with shallow visual reliance, which is critical for clinical deployment decisions.
2606.30201.decisionReason: SHOVIR is a named benchmark with a repeatable evaluation protocol using public datasets (MIMIC-CXR, PadChest-GR) and defined occlusion experiments, providing a credible path for other teams to run or inspect it.

2606.30124.description: SciIR-Bench evaluates text-to-image models on scientific image reasoning across three semiotic-aligned tracks: entity structure, scientific process, and scientific law. It uses an atomic checklist to convert scientific accuracy into verifiable fine-grained questions.
2606.30124.whyItMatters: Current text-to-image models lack rigorous evaluation for scientific imagery, which requires logical reasoning beyond visual fidelity. SciIR-Bench provides a structured protocol to measure such capabilities, aiding selection and development of models for scientific visualization tasks.
2606.30124.decisionReason: The paper introduces SciIR-Bench with a fixed dataset and protocol, provides a public evaluation interface and code for reproduction, and offers a clear scoring methodology via atomic checklists. This constitutes a standalone reusable benchmark.

2606.29887.description: SafePyramid evaluates in-context policy guardrailing across 1,000 multi-turn conversations and 3,000 application-specific policies containing 61,699 natural-language rules, organized into three hierarchical capability levels (L0, L1, L2). Scoring is based on violated-rule set prediction with metrics RMR and RDR, and the evaluation harness supports any API or local model.
2606.29887.whyItMatters: SafePyramid addresses the gap in evaluating guardrails under application-specific policies rather than fixed taxonomies, providing a structured test for rule understanding, dependency resolution, and adaptation to novel frameworks. It enables direct comparison of frontier LLMs and configurable guardrails on a realistic safety task.
2606.29887.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a fixed public dataset with 1,000 conversations and 3,000 policies, a clear evaluation protocol (per-policy and per-rule), and a public evaluation harness with leaderboard metrics, ensuring a stable scoring contract and reusable path.

2606.29920.description: RuVerBench evaluates LLM-as-a-judge reliability for rubric verification in agentic scenarios. It includes 2,458 instances across deep research and agentic coding, each with a model-generated output, a rubric, and a human-annotated label indicating rubric satisfaction.
2606.29920.whyItMatters: Rubric-based scoring with LLM judges is common but under-validated, especially for agentic outputs. RuVerBench provides a reusable benchmark to compare judge models and strategies, enabling decisions on model selection and scoring protocol.
2606.29920.decisionReason: The benchmark is a named, fixed dataset with a clear evaluation contract (human labels) and a public code repository enabling local reproduction and inspection.

2606.29937.description: REPAIR-Bench evaluates robot error perception and recovery in human-robot interaction. It includes 214 interaction trials from 41 participants with four induced failure types, synchronized facial action units, head pose, speech transcripts, and post-interaction reports. Three tasks cover failure detection across sessions, failure-type classification, and recovery prediction.
2606.29937.whyItMatters: REPAIR-Bench addresses the lack of unified benchmarks for HRI failures, enabling standardized evaluation of failure detection, classification, and recovery prediction. This supports the development of adaptive and trustworthy robot systems and provides a comparison baseline for future research.
2606.29937.decisionReason: The paper presents a new benchmark with a defined dataset and evaluation protocol. It includes multiple tasks with clear metrics, and provides the dataset for reuse, fulfilling the criteria for a public reusable benchmark.

2606.30262.description: OAO-AttackBench is a set of counterfactual prompts for one-and-only objects, used to evaluate text-to-image alignment in a specific study.
2606.30262.whyItMatters: The benchmark supports evaluating prompt adherence for concepts with strong visual priors, but it is introduced primarily to validate the proposed method and lacks a standalone public comparison path.
2606.30262.decisionReason: The benchmark is introduced in the paper to evaluate the proposed method, and no official code or downloadable dataset link is provided; the public project page only shows the concept and not a reusable benchmark artifact.

2606.29700.description: NL-PDDL-Bench evaluates natural-language-to-PDDL specification generation. It consists of multi-domain instances from IPC domains with planner-verified executability, difficulty scaled by object count, and a suite for parseability, solvability, and plan-level consistency.
2606.29700.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the lack of standardized evaluation for LLM-generated planning specifications, with an emphasis on executability and verifiability. It provides a reproducible basis for assessing model reliability in safety-sensitive planning applications, where incorrect formalization can lead to unsafe outcomes.
2606.29700.decisionReason: Public benchmark with available code and data, clear evaluation protocol, and planner-verified scoring. It is intended for reusable comparison by other teams.

2606.30026.description: MuseBench evaluates multimodal large language models on intent-level understanding of audiovisual arts, covering cinematic arts, static visual arts, stage performing arts, and game arts with 4,016 questions in single- and multi-select formats.
2606.30026.whyItMatters: Existing video and multimodal benchmarks mostly test perceptual recognition, leaving artistic intent and creative reasoning unevaluated. MuseBench measures a distinct capability gap, providing a reference for progress in creative-domain expertise.
2606.30026.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a fixed dataset, scoring metrics, and public code and data; provides a clear evaluation protocol for other teams to run or inspect.

2606.30182.description: MirrorCode evaluates AI agents on reimplementing entire software projects from behavior only, matching outputs on end-to-end tests across 25 programs spanning Unix utilities, data serialization, bioinformatics, interpreters, static analysis, cryptography, and compression.
2606.30182.whyItMatters: Existing coding benchmarks focus on shorter tasks, while long-horizon reimplementation remains hard to compare. MirrorCode provides a standardized, repeatable measure of autonomous software engineering capability.
2606.30182.decisionReason: Named benchmark with public repository, harness, task definitions, and scoring contract; designed for reuse and comparison across models.

2606.30371.description: MaDI-Bench evaluates end-to-end data integration pipelines across schema matching, value normalization, entity matching, and conflict resolution.
2606.30371.whyItMatters: Data integration tasks are often evaluated piecemeal; an end-to-end benchmark could support comparison of holistic pipelines.
2606.30371.decisionReason: No official links or artifact evidence provided to confirm public availability or reusable protocol.

2606.30256.description: EMPATH evaluates safety of emotional-support chatbots via auditor-generated multi-turn conversations scored on 19 metrics across crisis handling, therapeutic quality, conversational integrity, emotional safety, and cultural adaptation.
2606.30256.whyItMatters: Safety evaluation for emotional-support chatbots needs multilingual, multi-turn metrics; EMPATH appears to address that gap.
2606.30256.decisionReason: No public artifacts or official links are supplied to verify the benchmark's availability or scoring contract.

2608.00018.description: CITBench evaluates LLMs on interactive tabular data processing, covering table matching, cleaning, augmentation, and transformation across 18 task types and 1,296 instances.
2608.00018.whyItMatters: Tabular data processing benchmarks often focus on single-turn reasoning; interactive multi-turn settings remain underevaluated.
2608.00018.decisionReason: No official links or artifact evidence provided to confirm the benchmark's public availability or reusable protocol.

2606.29685.description: CAREBench evaluates language models on upstream child-safety risks with 500 prompts across twelve categories, assessing recognition, refusal, de-escalation, and redirection.
2606.29685.whyItMatters: Child-safety evaluation often focuses on explicit material; CAREBench targets earlier risk scenarios, which could help developers identify policy gaps.
2606.29685.decisionReason: No official links or artifact evidence are provided to verify the benchmark's availability or evaluation protocol.

2606.29445.description: VG-GUI-Bench evaluates MLLM-based GUI agents on following video tutorials to complete interactive tasks, with 1,000 long-horizon test cases and four metrics.
2606.29445.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses video-guided agentic tasks, complementing VideoQA benchmarks for procedural knowledge transfer.
2606.29445.decisionReason: Primarily supports the paper's proposed TASKER keyframe extraction method; the benchmark itself lacks a standalone comparison protocol and is tied to the paper's findings.

2606.29278.description: Complexity Ceiling Benchmark evaluates sequential reasoning decay with depth scaling across grounded spatial state-tracking, symbolic pointer manipulation, and transitive relational inference.
2606.29278.whyItMatters: It quantifies reasoning degradation with step count, which could inform model development for long-horizon tasks.
2606.29278.decisionReason: Primarily used to demonstrate the paper's decay model; lacks a public reusable artifact or standalone comparison path.

2606.29247.description: Evaluates vision-language-action models in laparoscopic surgical robotics across 8 tasks (atomic, conditional, composite) on the SurRoL simulator, using action accuracy and semantic consistency metrics.
2606.29247.whyItMatters: Fills the lack of standardized surgical VLA benchmarks, enabling comparison of autoregressive vs. flow-matching models and identifying physical bottlenecks like limited field of view.
2606.29247.decisionReason: Provides a named benchmark with hierarchical task taxonomy, multi-dimensional scoring, and public code/dataset links enabling reproducible evaluation.

2606.29592.description: STEMGym is an open-source Gymnasium benchmark of 15 physics-simulated STEM worlds across five materials and four characterization tasks, scored by DEC-AUC.
2606.29592.whyItMatters: Addresses the need to evaluate perception, navigation, and planning trade-offs in autonomous electron microscopy under dose budgets.
2606.29592.decisionReason: No official code or dataset links provided; artifacts unclear, preventing verification of reproducibility.

2606.29537.description: Evaluates computer-use agents on 108 long-horizon real-world workflows across everyday and professional tasks, scored by binary completion at 500 steps and partial scores.
2606.29537.whyItMatters: Captures long-horizon, dynamic, and hidden-state challenges absent in prior benchmarks, revealing that agents fail on constraint tracking and mid-task information.
2606.29537.decisionReason: Named benchmark with active release, public code, task files, assets, and documented evaluation protocol; ongoing versioned releases support model comparison.

2607.22658.description: StanceBench evaluates interpersonal stance in conversational speech across 9 dimensions using LLM-as-a-judge on the Seamless Interaction corpus.
2607.22658.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in benchmarks for prosody and interactional nuance in speech-to-speech models, focusing on judge bias and robustness.
2607.22658.decisionReason: Primarily supports a paper's finding on LLM-as-a-judge; lacks standalone public comparison track and clear reproducibility artifacts.

2606.27828.description: Evaluates video temporal-logical reasoning in multimodal LLMs across 25 fine-grained task categories, with difficulty-controlled final-answer scoring and intermediate-state diagnostics.
2606.27828.whyItMatters: Isolates temporal-logical capabilities from static recognition, revealing significant human-model gaps and providing a scalable testbed for analysis.
2606.27828.decisionReason: Provides fixed dataset with public Hugging Face access, evaluation scripts, and leaderboard; repeatable protocol with intermediate-state verification.

2606.28480.description: Evaluates terminal-use agents on 120 real-world tasks across five families (document editing, email, web info, scientific/engineering workflows) using execution-based scoring.
2606.28480.whyItMatters: Provides a broad, realistic terminal benchmark beyond coding, showing frontier agents achieve only 65.8% success, highlighting gaps in general-purpose digital work.
2606.28480.decisionReason: Named benchmark with public code, evaluation harness, leaderboard, and deterministic setup scripts; documented execution-based protocol and ongoing comparisons.

2606.27876.description: Evaluates spatial intelligence in low-altitude UAV scenarios across 14 task types covering semantic discrimination, spatial relations, collaboration, and motion understanding, with 7 input configurations and 9 answer formats.
2606.27876.whyItMatters: Targets under-evaluated 3D spatial and multi-view reasoning in UAV benchmarks, revealing bottlenecks in cross-view association and geometric reasoning for current VLMs.
2606.27876.decisionReason: Provides public dataset with annotations, code for inference and task-specific evaluation, and 4,331 instances; clear evaluation protocol and reproducible path.

2607.16243.description: Evaluates robustness of multimodal small language models for industrial anomaly detection across open-ended queries and visual degradations, using multiple-choice accuracy and LLM-judged open-ended responses.
2607.16243.whyItMatters: Assesses deployability of compact models in real-world industrial conditions, identifying failure modes like fragile grounding and hallucination on ill-posed queries.
2607.16243.decisionReason: Provides public code, dataset links, and evaluation scripts; fixed benchmark with human-validated questions and clear scoring metrics.

2606.27826.description: NormAct evaluates embodied agents on 550 TongSim scenarios where the same goal permits norm-compliant or norm-violating action sequences, testing whether agents infer and apply scene-relevant social norms during ordinary tasks.
2606.27826.whyItMatters: NormAct addresses the gap between goal achievement and proactive norm compliance, providing a way to assess whether embodied agents respect unstated social norms without prompting, which is critical for real-world deployment.
2606.27826.decisionReason: Artifacts for public reuse or scoring are not supplied; the benchmark is only described in the paper, so reuse or comparison is not currently verifiable.

2606.28556.description: IMCBench evaluates multimodal LLMs in image-grounded, multi-turn medical conversations, scoring safety, accuracy, and uncertainty use on a 1-5 scale.
2606.28556.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in medical AI benchmarks by combining clinical images with multi-turn dialogue, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy alongside patient safety and uncertainty management.
2606.28556.decisionReason: No official benchmark artifacts or public access path provided; the description is insufficient for a standalone public benchmark decision.

2606.27999.description: HumanMoveVQA evaluates video MLLMs on reasoning about human trajectory and orientation changes in videos, using a first-frame anchored world coordinate system and 10K question-answer pairs across seven reasoning categories.
2606.27999.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks fail to probe global human motion in space over time; HumanMoveVQA targets this gap, but without accessible data or code its practical value for model comparison remains unclear.
2606.27999.decisionReason: Benchmark artifacts (code, dataset) not provided; only paper text with no official links to data or evaluation scripts, making repeatable use by other teams uncertain.

2606.28514.description: GPTNT evaluates multimodal agents on real-time collaborative bomb defusal in the game Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, requiring asynchronous communication under time pressure and information asymmetry. Success is measured by defusing procedurally generated bombs.
2606.28514.whyItMatters: Current benchmarks isolate collaboration components; GPTNT captures time pressure, information asymmetry, and imperfect communication together, providing a realistic test for multimodal systems that current evaluations leave unmeasured.
2606.28514.decisionReason: Defined benchmark with repeatable evaluation (procedural bombs, live countdown) and comparable scoring (defusal success), offering public project site and code release for reuse.

2606.27669.description: DiscoBench evaluates search agents on clarification-aware deep search, covering 211 samples and 463 ambiguity instances across 11 domains, with four ambiguity types, measuring task utility, ambiguity detection, interaction strategy, and cost efficiency.
2606.27669.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the gap in evaluating search agents' ability to handle ambiguous and underspecified queries, which is common in real-world search. It assesses proactive clarification and interaction efficiency, offering practical value for improving agent decision-making in complex information-seeking tasks.
2606.27669.decisionReason: The abstract describes the benchmark but provides no official artifact link (e.g., code or dataset) to run or inspect it. Public reuse path is unclear, and the scoring contract is not fully defined. Therefore, defer while awaiting access to the benchmark artifacts.

2606.28593.description: Animation2Code evaluates temporal visual reasoning in video-to-code generation. It includes 1,069 web animation videos with corresponding HTML/CSS/JavaScript implementations, and uses appearance and temporal similarity metrics to assess model performance.
2606.28593.whyItMatters: Animation2Code addresses the lack of benchmarks for temporal dynamics in visual-to-code tasks. It provides a way to measure both visual fidelity and temporal alignment, which is crucial for applications requiring precise animation reconstruction.
2606.28593.decisionReason: The paper defines a benchmark with a clear evaluation object (video-to-code generation) and a comparable scoring contract using two metrics. The dataset and code are publicly available, providing a credible path for other teams to run or inspect it.

2606.28049.description: AirGroundBench evaluates multi-view spatial intelligence in multimodal large language models through UAV-UGV collaborative tasks, including 62,000 dual-view multiple-choice questions and 115 navigation episodes across 11 simulated environments.
2606.28049.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the gap in assessing geometric consistency across heterogeneous views, providing a structured evaluation for capabilities like cross-view alignment and spatial reasoning that are critical for embodied decision-making.
2606.28049.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a clear evaluation protocol, a fixed dataset with annotations, and a public path for reuse, meeting the criteria for a public reusable benchmark despite lacking a leaderboard.

2606.26984.description: Evaluates unified multimodal models on joint understanding and generation across four dimensions: internal consistency, understanding-guided generation, generation-guided understanding, and mutual enhancement, using 2,169 task samples.
2606.26984.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks assess understanding and generation in isolation, missing the synergy between them. This benchmark provides a diagnostic and human-aligned evaluation to measure and compare integrated capabilities, aiding model development.
2606.26984.decisionReason: Public benchmark with available data, code, and evaluation scripts, providing a fixed protocol and comparable scoring for other teams to run.

2606.26654.description: SocialPersona evaluates multimodal LLMs on recovering revealed preferences from longitudinal social-media timelines and using them in dialogue. It includes 171 user timelines, 2,597 human-verified preference tags across seven domains, and supports profile construction and response generation tasks.
2606.26654.whyItMatters: Existing personalization benchmarks rely on explicitly stated preferences; SocialPersona tests inference from natural multimodal traces, a harder capability. It provides a reusable benchmark for measuring progress on long-horizon user modeling and personalized dialogue.
2606.26654.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear evaluation object (social-media timelines), tasks, and human-verified annotations. Public dataset and protocol available via Hugging Face.

2606.26563.description: scBench-Long evaluates long-horizon single-cell biology reasoning. Agents must recover scientific conclusions from raw or near-raw data without prescribed methods. It contains 21 evaluations spanning diverse biological contexts, with deterministic grading and trajectory rubrics.
2606.26563.whyItMatters: Existing AI-biology benchmarks measure broad knowledge or local steps; scBench-Long assesses end-to-end scientific claim production. It provides a reusable evaluation for long-horizon reasoning in single-cell data analysis.
2606.26563.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear evaluation object (single-cell data workflows), repeatable scoring via deterministic grading, and public dataset/protocol available.

2606.26968.description: RedVox is a multilingual safety and fairness benchmark for speech models, built on real voices. It covers unsafe and unfair stereotypical requests across five languages and evaluates models under naturalistic conditions.
2606.26968.whyItMatters: Speech models are deployed globally but safety evaluations are mostly English-only. RedVox provides a reusable benchmark to assess cross-lingual safety gaps and the impact of spoken input.
2606.26968.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear evaluation object (speech model outputs on unsafe/biased requests), defined scoring contract, and public availability.

2606.26551.description: PhyEditBench evaluates physics-aware image editing. It includes 238 real-world instances and 35 synthetic anti-physics instances across 12 physical subclasses, with VLM-based scoring on consistency, instruction following, physical plausibility, and image quality.
2606.26551.whyItMatters: Image editing benchmarks often overlook physics reasoning; PhyEditBench provides a reusable evaluation to measure physical coherence in edited outputs, important for real-world applications.
2606.26551.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear evaluation object (image editing tasks), defined metrics and scoring protocol, and public code/data repository.

2606.26947.description: OmniRef-Bench is introduced in the paper but primarily serves to evaluate the proposed DyRef method. It is not presented as a standalone public benchmark.
2606.26947.decisionReason: The benchmark is introduced as part of a method paper and lacks a clear public reuse path for independent comparison.

2606.27047.description: NuclearQAv2 evaluates LLMs on nuclear engineering knowledge with approximately 1,240 QA pairs covering boolean, numeric, and verbal questions. It uses structured prompting for automated question generation and response evaluation.
2606.27047.whyItMatters: Technical domains like nuclear engineering require reliable LLM evaluation. NuclearQAv2 provides a scalable benchmark to assess factual knowledge, quantitative reasoning, and conceptual understanding in this domain.
2606.27047.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear evaluation object (QA pairs), defined scoring contract, and public dataset availability.

2606.27537.description: MemoBench evaluates world modeling in video generation via a disappear-and-reappear paradigm. It includes 360 ground-truth clips and an evaluation suite with automated metrics and VQA across four diagnostic pillars.
2606.27537.whyItMatters: Current benchmarks assess memory consistency only when objects remain visible; MemoBench tests object recovery after occlusion in dynamic scenes, providing a reusable diagnostic for world models.
2606.27537.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear evaluation object (video generation), defined metrics and protocol, and public code/data repository.

2606.26525.description: LCS-Bench is a theory-scale benchmark for auto-formalization in logics for computer science. It includes 327 textbook items, over 4,076 Lean declarations, and supports five evaluation tracks with definitional equivalence checkers.
2606.26525.whyItMatters: Auto-formalization at theory scale remains challenging. LCS-Bench provides a reusable benchmark to measure consistency, faithfulness, and correctness of formalization systems, enabling progress in scalable verification.
2606.26525.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear evaluation object (auto-formalization tasks), defined scoring protocol, and public dataset availability.

2606.27187.description: Evaluates harmful video understanding in large multimodal models using 1,379 videos and 4,137 multiple-choice questions across three hierarchical dimensions: Observable Evidence, Clip-Internal Meaning, and Beyond-Clip Reasoning.
2606.27187.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap of shallow binary classification in harmful video benchmarks by testing deep contextual understanding, and the absence of explanatory rationales, providing a diagnostic tool for model evaluation.
2606.27187.decisionReason: Lacks evidence of public availability for download or execution; only paper and HuggingFace page links provided without dataset repository. Artifact evidence empty.

2606.27079.description: A diagnostic safety benchmark for vision-language-action models, evaluating policies across physical interaction, instruction, and perception safety with cumulative cost and risk exposure metrics.
2606.27079.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses the lack of systematic safety evaluation for embodied VLA models, offering process-level risk metrics and a taxonomy to localize failure sources, which supports model selection and safety improvements.
2606.27079.decisionReason: No public artifacts or code links provided to verify a reusable benchmark implementation.

2606.27128.description: FlameVQA is a multiple-choice visual question answering benchmark for UAV-based wildfire monitoring, built on FLAME 3 with paired RGB and radiometric thermal images. It includes 34 questions per image across six capability groups, covering detection, localization, coverage estimation, cross-modal reasoning, and flight planning. Labels are generated via MLLM assistance, deterministic thermal rules, and human auditing. The dataset and code are open-source.
2606.27128.whyItMatters: FlameVQA addresses the lack of benchmarks for evaluating vision-language models in safety-critical wildfire scenarios where RGB-only interpretation is insufficient. It provides a standardized evaluation for capabilities like smoke detection and coverage estimation, which are critical for practical deployment of MLLMs in disaster monitoring.
2606.27128.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a fixed dataset and evaluation protocol with publicly available code and data, making it reusable by other teams for model comparison. It has a clear scoring contract through multiple-choice questions and a credible public path via the GitHub repository.

2606.27499.description: DMV-Bench evaluates visual memory of multimodal agents in an interactive shopping environment with 1,000 product variants. Agents run autonomous sessions and must recall cued product images via exact URL match, with text leakage controlled.
2606.27499.whyItMatters: Existing agent memory benchmarks focus on text; DMV-Bench isolates visual memory needs in interactive settings, offering a controlled protocol for comparing agent architectures on pixel-based recall across varying session lengths.
2606.27499.decisionReason: Public benchmark with released code and dataset, clear scoring contract (exact URL match), and reproducible interactive environment.

2606.26602.description: DiCoBench evaluates multimodal LLMs on multi-image fine-grained perception using high-resolution (up to 2K) image pairs. It includes 765 multiple-choice questions across two tracks: differential and commonality visual cues, covering 8 perception tasks, with exact-match scoring.
2606.26602.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks rely on explicit textual cues or low resolution, whereas DiCoBench targets autonomous discovery of subtle visual cues in high-resolution pairs. It provides a challenging testbed with a large human-model performance gap, aiding progress in complex multi-image understanding.
2606.26602.decisionReason: The benchmark is publicly released with evaluation code and dataset on GitHub and Hugging Face, includes a clear scoring protocol, and provides instructions for reproduction. It defines a repeatable evaluation object with public reuse path.

2606.26443.description: WatchAct evaluates robot manipulation from observed human behavior. Each instance pairs a human-action video and a language instruction with an aligned simulator scene and an executable LIBERO task. It covers 3,000 long-horizon instances across 14 tasks in four capability domains: Event Grounding, Procedural Reasoning, Implicit Intent Inference, and Episodic Reasoning. The evaluation protocol separately measures video-to-plan reasoning, policy execution under oracle plans, and full task completion, in simulation and on a Franka Research 3 robot.
2606.26443.whyItMatters: Existing manipulation benchmarks typically evaluate from a single current image, lacking grounding in observed human behavior. WatchAct fills this gap by assessing robots' ability to reason about events, procedures, intents, and scene changes from video, which is critical for real-world human-robot collaboration. It provides a disentangled evaluation to isolate reasoning and execution failures, offering practical value for developing and comparing systems.
2606.26443.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a clearly defined evaluation object (robot manipulation from video), a scoring contract (success rate, plan SR, task SR), and a public dataset and code link, making it reusable by other teams.

2606.26029.description: TriViewBench evaluates multimodal LLMs on multi-view structural reasoning using synthetic 3D scenes with controlled object count and occlusion. It comprises 1,923 scenes and over 14,000 QA pairs across four complexity levels and three reasoning categories: Local Decision, Object Counting, and Global Recovery.
2606.26029.whyItMatters: TriViewBench provides controlled complexity scaling to isolate structural reasoning capabilities in MLLMs, revealing distinct failure modes and bottlenecks. It enables systematic comparison of models on multi-view spatial reasoning, informing targeted improvements.
2606.26029.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a fixed set of scenes and QA pairs with a unified prompting protocol; the public paper and data availability indicate a path for reuse by other teams.

2606.25819.description: ToolBench-X evaluates tool-using agents on multi-step tasks with executable tools and automatic scoring, in environments that include recoverable reliability hazards such as specification drift, invocation errors, execution failures, output drift, and cross-source conflicts.
2606.25819.whyItMatters: Existing tool-use benchmarks assume stable tool environments, leaving a gap in evaluating agent performance under realistic unreliability. ToolBench-X provides a way to measure and compare agents' ability to diagnose and recover from tool hazards, which is crucial for practical deployment.
2606.25819.decisionReason: Benchmark defines a repeatable evaluation with canonical answers and automatic scoring, provides public code and data, and allows other teams to run it via the provided harness.

2606.25877.description: TacVerse is a multi-sensor dataset and benchmark for cross-sensor vision-based tactile perception, containing 106,800 tactile images from seven vision-based tactile sensors. It supports shape classification, grating classification, and force regression tasks, with evaluation under within-sensor, zero-shot cross-sensor, and few-shot adaptation settings.
2606.25877.whyItMatters: TacVerse fills a gap in evaluating generalization across tactile sensor designs, which is crucial for real-world robot deployment. It enables systematic study of sensor shift, data-efficient adaptation, and self-supervised learning in tactile perception, providing a controlled testbed for improving cross-sensor robustness.
2606.25877.decisionReason: Provides a fixed dataset with defined tasks and protocols, accessible via arXiv and official links, allowing other teams to run or inspect. It is not tied to a single paper's claim but offers a reusable evaluation resource.

2606.25634.description: SSMNBench is a diagnostic benchmark for cross-view human and human-object understanding, comprising 3,300 QA pairs categorized into Single-View Sufficiency (SVS) and Multi-View Necessity (MVN) tasks. It evaluates multimodal LLMs by perturbing view availability to assess distraction robustness and cross-view evidence integration.
2606.25634.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in evaluating genuine cross-view synthesis versus reliance on single-image semantics in MLLMs. It provides a rigorous framework for diagnosing limitations in cross-view understanding, guiding development of multimodal architectures for complex scenes.
2606.25634.decisionReason: Benchmark with fixed dataset and tasks, code available on GitHub, enabling other teams to run and inspect. It serves as a public evaluation tool for cross-view understanding, not just a one-off probe.

2606.28406.description: SciDraw-Bench is a benchmark for scientific figure generation, with 32 tasks across eight figure types and ten disciplines. Each task pairs a natural-language prompt with a machine-checkable specification, and evaluation uses four dimensions: Text Fidelity, Semantic Correctness, Structural Quality, and Convention Adherence.
2606.28406.whyItMatters: Fills the gap in evaluating scientific figure generation, which requires correct labels and diagrammatic structure beyond natural-image composition. It provides a protocol for measuring usability of generated figures, aiding development of domain-specific generative systems.
2606.28406.decisionReason: Offers a defined benchmark with tasks and evaluation protocol, and is described as a benchmark with machine-checkable specs. While details may not be fully released, it is designed as a reusable evaluation resource with ongoing validation.

2606.26094.description: RevengeBench is a benchmark for recovering code-space policies from behavioral traces. It includes 75 LLM-generated policies across five game environments, where a learner designs behavioral probes and submits executable hypotheses, evaluated using continuous action-distance metrics.
2606.26094.whyItMatters: Addresses the inverse problem of inferring hidden decision programs from observations, relevant to opponent modeling and policy interpretability. It provides a tractable testbed for studying how controlled experiments improve code-space recovery.
2606.26094.decisionReason: Defined as a benchmark with fixed set of policies and evaluation metrics, aiming for repeatable comparison. Public path is via paper description; although no explicit code link, it is intended as a reusable benchmark.

2608.00012.description: Obshazard-bench is a real-time benchmark for disaster intelligence, integrating raw satellite and ground-station data. It covers 8 disaster categories and 28 sub-categories across 60+ countries, with VQA samples and a three-stage evaluation taxonomy: Predictive Crisis Anticipation, Active Evolution Reasoning, and Multi-faceted Impact Quantification.
2608.00012.whyItMatters: Fills the gap in evaluating MLLMs for operational disaster response, which require real-time reasoning from raw observation streams. It provides a realistic testbed for assessing decision-support capabilities in evolving emergencies.
2608.00012.decisionReason: Provides a defined benchmark with datasets and protocols, designed for repeatable evaluation. It is a standalone public benchmark for disaster intelligence, with a clear evaluation taxonomy.

2606.26458.description: MKG-RAG-Bench is a benchmark for retrieval in multimodal knowledge graph-augmented generation, constructed from two knowledge graphs (general and medical) with QA datasets supporting controlled evaluation of retrieval and generation. It uses an LLM-based curation pipeline for structurally grounded queries.
2606.26458.whyItMatters: Isolates retrieval as a first-class evaluation target in MKG-RAG, addressing the challenge of heterogeneous multimodal knowledge. It provides a foundation for diagnosing retrieval limitations and improving end-to-end RAG systems.
2606.26458.decisionReason: Defined as a benchmark with fixed datasets and tasks, aiming for evaluating retrieval in MKG-RAG. It is a reusable public benchmark with a clear protocol.

2606.25402.description: LibEvoBench is a multi-task benchmark for evaluating code generation models on API evolution across versions of Python libraries. It includes tasks spanning multiple library versions and introduces the Software Evolution Understanding Score (SEUS) to measure version-specific knowledge consistency.
2606.25402.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in evaluating models on version-specific API knowledge, which is critical for real-world software maintenance. It highlights limitations of current training on temporally mixed corpora and motivates temporally grounded learning.
2606.25402.decisionReason: Provides a benchmark with defined tasks and a specific metric, intended for comparing models. It is a reusable public benchmark for code generation.

2606.25984.description: InvestPhilBench is a multi-layer benchmark for evaluating procedural reasoning in investment philosophy, spanning eight cognitive tiers from principle identification to novel framework extrapolation. It includes principle cards, decision-framework cards, and QA questions, with an automated scoring pipeline (BASP) and five algorithmic metrics.
2606.25984.whyItMatters: Fills the gap in testing whether LLMs can accurately reconstruct and apply expert procedural decision frameworks. Provides a reproducible method for scoring procedural reasoning, with a metric (GRA) that exposes deficits hidden by composite scores.
2606.25984.decisionReason: Defined as a benchmark with fixed data and scoring method, designed for ongoing evaluation. It provides public artifacts and a leaderboard in future, but even v0.6 is a reusable benchmark with methodology.

2606.25491.description: HG-Bench evaluates page-aware, two-level answer-region grounding: given multi-page handwritten homework images, models must localize complete answer regions and ordered step-level subregions, with question- and step-level boxes under a hierarchical constraint.
2606.25491.whyItMatters: Automated homework assessment needs both answer recognition and spatial grounding of reasoning steps. Prior benchmarks miss page-aware, multi-level localization; HG-Bench provides a reproducible protocol to measure this capability gap across models.
2606.25491.decisionReason: Named benchmark with 500 annotated samples, clear evaluation protocol with FA and FSm scores, and paper/report links providing reproducibility details.

2606.25915.description: FunPiQ is a benchmark for pixel-level fundus image quality assessment with pixel-level annotations for anatomical visibility, using a three-class scheme (good, usable, bad). It also introduces EFIQA-CP, an explainable method trained with pseudo-labels.
2606.25915.whyItMatters: Existing FIQA benchmarks provide only image-level labels, limiting localized degradation analysis. FunPiQ enables task-agnostic explainable quality evaluation through pixel-level ground truth and offers a public dataset for method comparison.
2606.25915.decisionReason: Named benchmark with pixel-level annotations, downloadable dataset (Zenodo/GitHub), and code repository; clear evaluation protocol using pixel-wise classification.

2607.16229.description: FinBench is a benchmark for evaluating calibration and uncertainty in financial forecasting with time-gated tasks, requiring probability of positive return and 80% prediction interval, scored with Brier and Winkler scores.
2607.16229.whyItMatters: Financial forecasting agents risk overconfidence; FinBench addresses this by testing probabilistic calibration under temporal constraints, but its pilot scale limits immediate comparison value.
2607.16229.decisionReason: Paper reports only a small pilot run (one day, three tickers) and lacks a clear public release path for the benchmark; thus not yet a fully reusable evaluation.

2606.26216.description: CyberChainBench evaluates LLM-based agents on smart contract security across vulnerability detection, exploit generation, and patch synthesis, using 541 real exploit incidents with on-chain evaluation on historical forks.
2606.26216.whyItMatters: Smart contract security requires realistic, end-to-end evaluation of agent capabilities; CyberChainBench provides structured ground truth and economic impact metrics to measure practical effectiveness.
2606.26216.decisionReason: Named benchmark with 541 real incidents, clear scoring via economic impact and test oracles, and reproducible evaluation environments orchestrated by Harbor; paper provides methodology.

2606.26437.description: ConflictBench is a benchmark with ConflictScore metric to quantify how well models acknowledge conflicting evidence in grounding documents, decomposing responses into claims and labeling them against documents.
2606.26437.whyItMatters: Existing factuality metrics ignore coexisting contradictions; ConflictScore provides a nuanced measure over ConflictBench, offering a corrective feedback mechanism for improving truthfulness.
2606.26437.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined metric and dataset, but primarily supports the paper's proposed metric and experiments; public reuse path is not clearly established.

2606.25763.description: CaptureGuide-Bench evaluates capture-time photography guidance with two tasks: photographer-side composition decision/refinement and subject-side scene-conditioned pose recommendation, using metrics like IoU and plausibility.
2606.25763.whyItMatters: Existing aesthetic benchmarks focus on post-hoc cropping; CaptureGuide-Bench addresses missing capture-time guidance for both framing and subject pose, providing a structured dataset for development.
2606.25763.decisionReason: Named benchmark with two tasks and clear evaluation metrics; public dataset and code available via GitHub and Hugging Face links.

2606.25445.description: C3-Bench evaluates context-aware change captioning with 4,996 human-labeled image pairs across 51 real-world contexts, using an LLM-as-Judge framework scoring correctness, specificity, fluency, relevance, and a reversibility metric.
2606.25445.whyItMatters: Change captioning performance varies with domain; C3-Bench exposes systematic failures in conventional models and LMMs, providing a comprehensive benchmark to drive generalization and trustworthiness.
2606.25445.decisionReason: Named benchmark with 4,996 samples, clear evaluation framework with fine-grained dimensions, and public availability of code and dataset as stated.

2606.24256.description: Tailor-Bench evaluates visual world models on simulating irregular physical interactions with three scenario modes (regular, unconventional, impossible) and predictive/descriptive generation settings.
2606.24256.whyItMatters: Current benchmarks focus on common interactions; Tailor-Bench exposes the long-tail gap in physical world modeling, testing generalization and constraint awareness beyond typical scenarios.
2606.24256.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear scenario modes and evaluation protocol; public code repository and detailed generation/annotation pipeline.

2606.24145.description: T2D-Bench evaluates LLM outputs for type 2 diabetes against evidence constraints using a multi-layer clinical-lifestyle knowledge graph, covering diagnosis, medication safety, and lifestyle conflicts across 100 structured vignettes.
2606.24145.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in evaluating whether LLM recommendations satisfy explicit clinical guidelines and justify lifestyle-related glycemic claims, providing a mechanism to detect unsupported omissions and improve verifier-level compliance.
2606.24145.decisionReason: No public code or dataset link provided; artifacts unclear, preventing verification of a clear public reuse path.

2606.24235.description: SP-Mind is an autonomous AI agent for spatial proteomics analysis, and SP-Bench is introduced for evaluation with 102 tasks across 18 categories.
2606.24235.whyItMatters: The benchmark appears tied to the agent's capabilities and lacks a standalone comparison path for other teams.
2606.24235.decisionReason: SP-Bench is presented as part of the SP-Mind system and lacks a standalone public comparison path.

2606.24648.description: ParaPairAudioBench evaluates LALMs as judges for paralinguistic speech across five dimensions with 5,175 audio pairs.
2606.24648.whyItMatters: Targets fine-grained paralinguistic distinctions that prior benchmarks overlook, enabling calibration-aware assessment of judge reliability.
2606.24648.decisionReason: No public artifacts or links provided, making the evaluation protocol and reuse path unclear.

2606.24530.description: NatureBench evaluates AI coding agents on 90 tasks distilled from Nature-family publications across 6 scientific domains, scoring against each paper's reported state of the art.
2606.24530.whyItMatters: Provides a standardized environment and public leaderboard to measure whether coding agents can achieve discovery-level performance on real scientific problems, addressing environment-fragmentation issues in prior benchmarks.
2606.24530.decisionReason: Public code, dataset, and leaderboard with submission instructions are available, indicating a clear path for others to run or inspect the benchmark.

2606.24200.description: MMed-Bench-IR evaluates multilingual medical information retrieval across 6 languages with three tasks: cross-lingual QA retrieval, concept discrimination, and evidence retrieval for RAG.
2606.24200.whyItMatters: Uncovers severe cross-lingual failures in biomedical encoders that English-only benchmarks miss, highlighting the need for multilingual capability measurement in clinical RAG.
2606.24200.decisionReason: No public artifacts or links provided; the evaluation protocol and reuse path are unclear.

2606.24595.description: MEMPROBE evaluates long-term memory in LLM agents by reconstructing hidden user-state from agent memory across 50 simulated users with 31 hidden dimensions each.
2606.24595.whyItMatters: Offers a direct measure of memory fidelity as an auditable artifact, distinct from downstream task success, potentially improving agent memory evaluation.
2606.24595.decisionReason: No public artifacts or links provided; the benchmark's standalone usability is unclear.

2606.24155.description: MedBench v5 evaluates clinical multimodal models across 63 tasks with process-oriented metrics including stressors and hallucination tracking.
2606.24155.whyItMatters: Addresses gaps in process visibility and hallucination detection in medical AI evaluation, offering a unified framework for capability profiling and stress testing.
2606.24155.decisionReason: No public artifacts or links provided; unclear if the benchmark is standalone and reusable by other teams.

2606.24829.description: GeoT2V-Bench evaluates 3D consistency in camera-prompted text-to-video models via 3D reconstruction, using metrics like static rendering error and flow agreement.
2606.24829.whyItMatters: Assesses whether generated videos can support explicit rigid 3D reconstruction, providing a diagnostic tool for a critical limitation of T2V models.
2606.24829.decisionReason: No public artifacts or links provided; the evaluation protocol and reuse path are unclear.

2607.09711.description: EvoClawBench evaluates whether an agent runtime can convert evidence from its own runs into reusable skills that improve fresh executions. It covers 100 tasks and 502 sub-problems across coding, data, office, security, operations, and domain-document workflows, comparing direct execution, pre-authored skills, and post-run skill summarization.
2607.09711.whyItMatters: The evaluation gap is assessing closed-loop skill learning in agents, where benefits are selective and cost-sensitive rather than automatic. The benchmark provides a decision value for runtime developers and users considering skill-authoring loops.
2607.09711.decisionReason: The benchmark is named and described, but no official links to a public benchmark repository or leaderboard are provided, and artifactEvidence is empty. Public reuse path is unclear.

2606.24422.description: EgoSAT evaluates vision-language models on egocentric video reasoning in streaming settings. It contains 1,997 videos (165 hours) and about 4,800 QA pairs covering retrospective, online, and prospective reasoning tasks.
2606.24422.whyItMatters: Serves as a unified benchmark for streaming egocentric interaction understanding, enabling assessment of temporal reasoning and confidence calibration in VLMs, which is crucial for reliable deployment in real-time applications.
