2606.01810.description: Causal-Plan-Bench evaluates embodied planning across four causal dimensions (executability, effects, composition, robustness) using 1,200 instances from 12 tasks, with MCQ and rubric-based scoring.
2606.01810.whyItMatters: Targets the gap where benchmarks reward linguistic prediction over physical causal reasoning, offering a diagnostic protocol to assess genuine physical agency and support training for grounded planning.
2606.01810.decisionReason: Official GitHub repository provides benchmark evaluation code and data validation scripts, enabling external reuse.

2606.01897.description: CASTER-Bench evaluates whether user-generated content achieves positive community resonance based on multimodal attributes, using human annotations across diverse categories.
2606.01897.whyItMatters: Expands quality assessment from visual fidelity to social engagement, providing a task for modeling community resonance rather than just aesthetic quality.
2606.01897.decisionReason: No artifact links or official benchmark access provided; cannot verify a public reusable path.

2606.02798.description: BehaviorBench evaluates personalized decision modeling from real-world behavioral traces, with belief and trade prediction tasks from prediction-market and on-chain records across 2,000 wallets.
2606.02798.whyItMatters: Provides a real-world alternative to simulated user benchmarks, testing whether personalization methods can use observed behavioral evidence effectively in decision-support settings.
2606.02798.decisionReason: No official artifact links or dataset access provided; public availability is unverified.

2606.07643.description: AVI-Bench evaluates omni-multimodal LLMs on audio-visual tasks across perception, understanding, and reasoning stages, with an extension probing primitive audio-visual sensation using unfamiliar low-semantic stimuli.
2606.07643.whyItMatters: Provides a structured way to measure joint audio-visual capabilities in multimodal models, which is currently under-evaluated.
2606.07643.decisionReason: No evidence of a public dataset, code, or leaderboard for others to run the benchmark; only a project page. Evaluation setup and scoring not fully specified.

2606.01961.description: AutoMedBench evaluates autonomous AI agents on end-to-end medical-AI research tasks spanning segmentation, image enhancement, VQA, report generation, and lesion detection. Tasks follow a five-stage workflow (Plan, Setup, Validate, Inference, Submit), with scoring based on both final task performance and stage-level rubric scores.
2606.01961.whyItMatters: Existing medical agent benchmarks focus on final outputs, obscuring failure points. AutoMedBench provides granular stage-level scoring and error analysis, enabling targeted assessment of agent capabilities and highlighting bottlenecks like verification and submission, which can guide improvement priorities in automated medical research systems.
2606.01961.decisionReason: Public code repository with evaluation instructions, hosted dataset, and live leaderboard provide a reusable path and comparable scoring contract.

2606.02240.description: AgentRedBench evaluates LLM agents against indirect prompt injection and underspecified-authorization attacks across 24 enterprise SaaS integrations. It defines 215 attack scenarios with immutable versioning, and tracks attack success rate (ASR) for models and defenses. Open-source codebase and schemas enable replay.
2606.02240.whyItMatters: Prior agent-security benchmarks cover limited integrations with static payloads, understating real-world exploitability. AgentRedBench provides a dynamic, maintainer-mediated evaluation to compare model and guard-rail effectiveness against evolving injection threats, supporting procurement and hardening decisions.
2606.02240.decisionReason: The paper defines a repeatable benchmark with a clear scoring contract (ASR on fixed scenarios), open codebase/schemas, and a credible path for others to run or inspect via the released codebase and maintainer-mediated channel.

2606.01322.description: TUKABENCH is a benchmark for jailbreak evaluation in seven African languages, extending JailbreakBench with human translations, cultural adaptations, and code-switched prompts. It assesses LLM safety in low-resource languages using metrics like Refused, Jailbroken, and Deflection, with human validation of LLM-as-a-judge.
2606.01322.whyItMatters: The benchmark addresses a gap in safety evaluation for low-resource African languages, showing that models are more vulnerable to jailbreak prompts in these languages. It could inform safer deployment of LLMs in multilingual contexts.
2606.01322.decisionReason: No official benchmark artifact, leaderboard, or public evaluation harness is provided; the paper describes the benchmark but lacks a clear public path for others to run or inspect it.

2606.01046.description: TravelEval evaluates LLM-powered travel planning agents in a realistic sandbox with accommodation pricing and intercity transport data, using six dimensions: accuracy, compliance, temporality, spatiality, economy, and utility. It simulates complete plans with API-integrated geographic information and queuing time.
2606.01046.whyItMatters: Existing travel planning benchmarks overemphasize constraint compliance, lack real-world data coverage, and miss global plan quality. TravelEval offers a multi-dimensional framework to compare agent planning capabilities, aiding model selection for complex travel tasks.
2606.01046.decisionReason: The paper describes a benchmark framework but does not provide artifact evidence, public leaderboard, or code repository links for others to run or inspect. The evaluation protocol lacks a clear scoring contract and public reuse path, making it unclear if it is a usable public benchmark.

2606.01498.description: TimeSage-MT evaluates agentic time series reasoning in multi-turn dialogues, covering 240 tasks and 2,680 turns across 8 domains, with a protocol and leaderboard for comparing systems.
2606.01498.whyItMatters: It fills a gap in benchmarking agentic time series analysis, which differs from single-step tasks, offering a way to assess multi-turn memory, uncertainty handling, and decision-making, with practical value for developing and comparing LLM agents.
2606.01498.decisionReason: Named benchmark with repeatable evaluation (multi-turn tasks, verifiable answers) and public leaderboard/protocol for comparison. Artifact evidence limited but official paper link supplied.

2606.02642.description: SVHalluc evaluates speech-vision hallucination in audio-visual large language models, focusing on semantic and temporal alignment between speech content and visual signals.
2606.02642.whyItMatters: Addresses a critical gap in evaluating audio-visual LLMs, as prior benchmarks ignored speech-induced hallucinations. Provides a systematic method to assess model grounding, aiding in model development and selection for multimodal applications.
2606.02642.decisionReason: The study presents a new benchmark with a defined protocol, datasets, and scoring, and provides a project page for inspection, meeting criteria for a public reusable benchmark.

2606.01317.description: SABER evaluates operational safety of LLM coding agents in stateful project workspaces. Agents perform realistic tasks, and safety is scored from the final environment state after action sequences. Violations are categorized by cause, enabling model-specific safety profile analysis.
2606.01317.whyItMatters: Existing safety benchmarks only check prompt refusal, missing the impact of action sequences on workspaces. SABER fills this gap by measuring environment-aware operational safety, offering a practical way to compare models on their ability to avoid harmful state changes in realistic coding tasks.
2606.01317.decisionReason: Public benchmark with available code, dataset, judging pipeline, and execution instructions. It provides a repeatable evaluation object and comparable scoring contract for other teams.

2606.01223.description: RefMem-Bench is a benchmark for reflective memory in long-horizon dialogue, containing 26K QA instances across eight reflective-memory dimensions and three task formats.
2606.01223.whyItMatters: It evaluates the ability of models to synthesize fragmented multimodal cues into high-level interpretations, going beyond explicit recall.
2606.01223.decisionReason: The benchmark is introduced as part of a paper proposing a method (REMIND) and lacks a standalone public comparison path or ongoing scoring infrastructure; it is a viewpoint probe.

2606.01016.description: PolySpeech-100 evaluates speech understanding in speech-large language models across 110 linguistic variants, including 19 Chinese dialects and over 80 low-resource languages, using tasks that assess semantic reasoning beyond transcription.
2606.01016.whyItMatters: Existing speech benchmarks are biased toward high-resource languages and focus on low-level recognition, limiting assessment of reasoning abilities and dialect robustness. PolySpeech-100 provides a broader coverage and a scoring protocol for comparing model performance on diverse speech understanding tasks.
2606.01016.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a clear evaluation object (speech understanding across 110 language variants), a defined scoring contract (accuracy from evaluation script), and a public leaderboard and code repository for other teams to run or inspect it.

2606.01132.description: HakushoBench is a Japanese chart and table VQA benchmark built from 33 governmental white papers, containing 2,053 images across over 10 image types with manually annotated QA pairs. It evaluates vision-language models on deep holistic understanding of charts and tables.
2606.01132.whyItMatters: HakushoBench addresses the scarcity of non-English benchmarks for chart and table understanding, providing a challenging evaluation for VLMs in Japanese document domains. It reveals a notable performance gap between open-weight and proprietary models, highlighting areas for improvement in multilingual document AI.
2606.01132.decisionReason: The paper defines a fixed dataset (2,053 images, QA pairs) with a clear task (VQA on charts and tables), a scoring metric (accuracy), and releases dataset and code, providing a public reuse path for other teams.

2606.01348.description: ChartArena is a bilingual benchmark for chart parsing covering eight chart families (bar, line, pie, radar, box plot, combination, flowchart, mind map) across three visual scenarios (digital, printed, hand-drawn). It uses a format-agnostic evaluation protocol with structure-aware metrics.
2606.01348.whyItMatters: Existing chart benchmarks cover limited chart types and ignore diagrammatic structures and real-world images. ChartArena provides a unified evaluation across diverse charts and scenarios, enabling assessment of model generalization and identifying capability gaps.
2606.01348.decisionReason: The benchmark has a clear evaluation object (chart parsing), a defined scoring contract (structure-aware metrics on canonical semantic spaces), and public code and data for reuse.

2606.01057.description: 3DCodeBench evaluates vision-language model agents on procedural 3D modeling by converting text and image references into Blender Python code. It includes 212 object categories with ground-truth scripts, and scores outputs on executability, image similarity (SigLIP-2/DINOv3), 3D shape distance (Chamfer/Uni3D), and LLM-as-judge, plus a human-preference ranking platform.
2606.01057.whyItMatters: There is no standardized way to compare model abilities in procedural 3D code generation. This benchmark provides a fixed protocol and dataset, enabling reproducible evaluation and comparison across models and coding-agent settings, useful for selecting models or guiding development of procedural modeling capabilities.
2606.01057.decisionReason: The paper and official links confirm a dedicated benchmark with a clear protocol, a released dataset, and an evaluation platform. The repository includes instructions for running tasks and scoring, and the data is publicly available on HuggingFace.

2606.00925.description: SkillVetBench is a two-stage security vetting benchmark for open agentic skill ecosystems, evaluating detection of malicious skills via semantic analysis and runtime verification in a sandbox. The benchmark is built from confirmed malicious skills in the OpenClaw ecosystem.
2606.00925.whyItMatters: Open agent platforms face supply-chain risks from malicious skills, but existing defenses lack a standardized evaluation. This benchmark addresses the gap in measuring both detection and runtime verification, offering practical value for improving security in agent ecosystems.
2606.00925.decisionReason: No official artifact or public code/data link provided; benchmark not accessible for reuse or inspection, so the public comparison path is unclear.

2606.24894.description: Evaluates related work generation as citation-centric scholarly positioning. Uses 100 peer-reviewed papers and a 1.09M-document retrieval corpus, with metrics for citation selection, contextual appropriateness, organization, and discourse structure.
2606.24894.whyItMatters: Fills the gap in RWG evaluation that relies on surface text similarity, offering a citation-centric testbed that aligns with expert judgment and reveals systematic limitations in current systems.
2606.24894.decisionReason: Public benchmark with released code and dataset, providing a clear evaluation protocol and metrics for citation decision-making.

2606.00451.description: ProtStructQA is an executable benchmark for protein structural question answering, with questions generated from DSL programs and answers obtained by executing on AlphaFold-predicted structures. Released 382.2K questions covering confidence, distances, PAE, solvent exposure, secondary structure, topology, and contacts.
2606.00451.whyItMatters: Provides a diagnostic testbed for when language models can map words to executable 3D structural measurements, with a denotation threshold between model sizes.
2606.00451.decisionReason: No official code or dataset link provided; artifact evidence absent, so public reuse path is unclear.

2607.20482.description: PersonaTrail evaluates personalized web agents using realistic browsing trajectories as user history, assessing preference inference and information recall. Operates in a managed open web environment with two tasks.
2607.20482.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in web agent benchmarks by capturing personalization from raw browsing history, moving beyond fully explicit prompts.
2607.20482.decisionReason: No official code or dataset links; public availability not established.

2606.00815.description: OmniEEG-Bench is a unified benchmark for EEG foundation models, organizing evaluation into six task families and unifying 54 EEG datasets. It provides a leaderboard and code repository.
2606.00815.whyItMatters: Standardizes evaluation of EEG foundation models across diverse tasks, revealing scaling-law behavior and the importance of pretraining data diversity.
2606.00815.decisionReason: Code repository is unverified and may not be publicly accessible; paper not yet published.

2606.00832.description: Momento benchmarks persistent agentic task completion in multi-session service environments, requiring agents to resolve temporal dependencies and evolving user goals across sessions.
2606.00832.whyItMatters: Highlights the gap in agent evaluation by focusing on multi-session history and misestimation of user state, which is critical for realistic human-agent interaction.
2606.00832.decisionReason: No official code or dataset links; public availability not established.

2606.00891.description: MMDG-Bench is a benchmark for multi-modal domain generalization, providing two frameworks (D2M and M2D) and unified protocols across action recognition and face anti-spoofing tasks. Includes code repository.
2606.00891.whyItMatters: Provides a principled foundation for MMDG research, with insights on framework choice and backbone effects, and offers design guidelines for multi-modal robustness.
2606.00891.decisionReason: The benchmark is a testbed for a paper's specific findings; code exists but public reuse path is not clearly established and is intended for internal use.

2606.00622.description: MM-Snowball is a benchmark for diagnosing hallucination snowballing in multimodal multi-turn dialogue, with fine-grained analysis. It includes data and code via a project page.
2606.00622.whyItMatters: Addresses the lack of benchmarks for error propagation in long-horizon interactions, and shows existing mitigation methods are ineffective, motivating new approaches.
2606.00622.decisionReason: The benchmark is primarily a viewpoint probe to support the paper's findings; no standalone public comparison path is provided.

2606.00793.description: MBench is a benchmark for memory capability of video world models, decomposing into entity, environment, and causal consistency with 12 sub-dimensions. Includes code, dataset, and leaderboard.
2606.00793.whyItMatters: Fills the gap in evaluating long-term state retention in video world models, providing a standardized benchmark to advance the field.
2606.00793.decisionReason: The benchmark is a testbed for the paper's findings rather than a standalone public comparison path.

2606.00750.description: A benchmark of 19 research papers with expert-built interactive systems for evaluating agents that convert PDFs into executable web applications.
2606.00750.whyItMatters: Supports evaluation of interactive system generation but relies on limited data and lacks documented public reuse.
2606.00750.decisionReason: Viewpoint probe primarily supports one paper's findings, lacks public reuse path, and evidence of benchmark infrastructure is absent.

2606.00644.description: Temporally controlled benchmark with 500 tasks across AI domains for forward-looking research judgment; includes offline knowledge bases and validation protocols.
2606.00644.whyItMatters: Could support evaluation of research agents in forecasting tasks, but current evidence is insufficient to establish credibility and public accessibility.
2606.00644.decisionReason: Public availability and scoring contract are not clearly specified; evidence of benchmark infrastructure for reuse is absent.

2606.00931.description: CV-Arena is a benchmark of 12K high-resolution image instruction pairs across 16 task types, with a human-AI collaborative preference protocol (Active Elo) for evaluating instructional computer vision problem solving.
2606.00931.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in evaluating diverse real-image editing tasks with professional constraints, providing a scalable and traceable evaluation resource for model comparison.
2606.00931.decisionReason: Provides a large-scale dataset, defined evaluation protocol, and public benchmark infrastructure; suitable for standalone reuse.

2606.00548.description: CAFOSat is a dataset of over 45,000 image patches with infrastructure-level annotations for CAFO mapping across 20 states, benchmarking models for infrastructure-aware agricultural monitoring.
2606.00548.whyItMatters: Provides a large-scale, infrastructure-aware benchmark for advancing CAFO mapping from remote sensing, addressing the lack of strongly annotated datasets in this domain.
2606.00548.decisionReason: Describes a large-scale, publicly reusable dataset with clear task and evaluation protocol; suitable for model comparison.

2606.00154.description: WebIGBench evaluates code generation for interactive webpages with 103 complex examples and 871 distinct actions, proposing an automated evaluation pipeline for interactive consistency.
2606.00154.whyItMatters: Fills the gap in benchmarking interactive webpage code generation, offering a public dataset and evaluation method for model comparison.
2606.00154.decisionReason: Provides a public benchmark with clear task and evaluation protocol; official code repository available for reuse.

2606.07595.description: VisualLeakBench is a 500-image benchmark for evaluating action-boundary propagation failures in vision-language agents, with stratified subsets and oracle diagnostics.
2606.07595.whyItMatters: Targets a specific safety failure mode in VLAs, but lacks clear public reuse path and scoring contract details.
2606.07595.decisionReason: Benchmark is primarily for investigation; public reuse and scoring are not fully specified.

2605.31113.description: TSM-Bench is a multilingual, multi-generator, multi-task benchmark for evaluating machine-generated text detectors on real-world Wikipedia editing tasks.
2605.31113.whyItMatters: Reveals performance drops in detectors on task-specific MGT, providing a foundation for developing robust detectors for UGC platforms.
2605.31113.decisionReason: Offers a benchmark with documented evaluation protocol and public availability; suitable for model comparison.

2605.31196.description: TouchSafeBench is a physics-grounded benchmark with 2,940 simulated episodes for evaluating collision grounding in vision-language models for safe human-robot collaboration.
2605.31196.whyItMatters: Targets a critical safety capability in embodied AI, but current evidence lacks public availability and scoring details.
2605.31196.decisionReason: Benchmark is not yet released publicly as stated; evidence of reuse path and scoring contract is incomplete.

2606.02624.description: TadA-Bench is a fixed-data replay benchmark derived from 31 wet-lab rounds of TadA directed evolution. Models rank ~1M protein, DNA, or RNA sequence variants appearing only in later rounds, with scores as Spearman, Recall@10%, and nDCG@10%.
2606.02624.whyItMatters: Standard random-split evaluation overestimates performance for iterative candidate prioritization. TadA-Bench provides a chronological replay protocol to measure whether models can transfer from earlier experimental rounds to future ones, a core requirement for agentic protein engineering.
2606.02624.decisionReason: Fixed splits and scoring metrics defined, with code, dataset, and leaderboard submission schema publicly available; official results for ICML 2026.

2605.31529.description: SVI-Bench evaluates vision-language models on strategic video intelligence using sports as a microworld. It includes 9 tasks across 4 pillars: perception, reasoning, simulation, and agency, using basketball, soccer, and hockey videos with annotated actions and reports.
2605.31529.whyItMatters: Existing video benchmarks lack verifiable ground truth for causal and strategic reasoning. SVI-Bench combines real-world multi-agent complexity with verifiable rules and outcomes, enabling evaluation of higher-level cognitive capabilities in video understanding.
2605.31529.decisionReason: Publicly available code and gated Hugging Face dataset with per-task evaluation protocols; many tasks with defined metrics, suitable for model comparison.

2606.00148.description: StemBind is a diagnostic benchmark with shared-stem questions to attribute failures in abstract visual reasoning. It includes perception, rule, and full tasks with stage annotations but no official code or dataset release.
2606.00148.whyItMatters: It aims to localize reasoning failures to specific sub-steps, potentially guiding improvements in multimodal models, but lacks a public path for independent verification.
2606.00148.decisionReason: No code, data, or official evaluation protocol provided, so it cannot be used for external comparison.

2605.31597.description: SOCO is a benchmark for semantic object correspondence with keypoint annotations across 100 categories and over 1M pairs. The evaluation is implemented within OmniProbe, which includes correspondence tasks among others.
2605.31597.whyItMatters: It provides a systematic evaluation for part-level understanding in vision models, but since it is part of a larger framework, it is not a standalone benchmark.
2605.31597.decisionReason: SOCO is a dataset incorporated into OmniProbe, which is a broader evaluation framework; the benchmark is not fully defined independently here.

2605.31478.description: PowerCodeBench is a benchmark generator for power system code generation, paired with an intervention method, but no artifacts are provided in this article.
2605.31478.whyItMatters: It addresses reliability of open-weight models for on-premise deployment, but the lack of a release prevents external use.
2605.31478.decisionReason: No code, data, or evaluation protocol is supplied, so it cannot be used as a public benchmark.

2606.00188.description: PaintBench is a procedurally generated benchmark for precise visual editing, covering 20 tasks across geometric, structural, color, and symbolic categories. Stable scoring uses pixel-level mIoU with fixed seeds.
2606.00188.whyItMatters: Procedural generation allows contamination-resistant evaluation of precise editing capabilities, with deterministic scoring that avoids human or LLM bias.
2606.00188.decisionReason: Public code, dataset generation, and evaluation scripts are provided; it is a fixed benchmark usable by others.

2605.30727.description: MosaicLeaks is a benchmark of 1,001 multi-hop research tasks to evaluate privacy leakage in deep research agents, but no artifacts are provided in this article.
2605.30727.whyItMatters: It addresses privacy risks in agentic workflows, but without a public release, external teams cannot use it.
2605.30727.decisionReason: No code, data, or evaluation protocol is supplied, so it cannot be used as a public benchmark.

2605.31031.description: GraphARC is a benchmark for abstract reasoning on graphs, generalizing ARC few-shot learning. No artifacts are provided in this article.
2605.31031.whyItMatters: It aims to evaluate relational reasoning in graph models, but lacks a public path for external evaluation.
2605.31031.decisionReason: No code or data is provided, preventing standalone use.

2608.12324.description: FMG-Bench evaluates English-language Christian theological triage and pastoral guidance in LLMs. It scores whether model responses match expected behaviors for triage levels: primary doctrine, secondary doctrine, prudential, and pastoral, with safety-related escalation appropriate to each scenario. The corpus includes 120 base scenarios plus 37 perturbation variants.
2608.12324.whyItMatters: Evaluates a niche but real usage area where models are asked for faith and care advice. Provides a structured scoring contract for safety-critical escalation and robustness to rephrasing, which are not covered by generic QA or safety benchmarks. Useful for developers testing models in contexts where human referral matters.
2608.12324.decisionReason: Benchmark defines a repeatable evaluation object (120 scenarios) and a scoring contract in the public repository. The public dataset and runner code provide a credible path for other teams to run or inspect the benchmark.

2605.31349.description: FBHM evaluates vision-language models on hateful meme detection across 25 rhetorical functionalities and 10 target communities, with 5,000 memes. Performance is measured by Macro-F1 score on this curated dataset.
2605.31349.whyItMatters: Existing hateful meme benchmarks confound rhetorical strategies with target community features, preventing causal evaluation of model vulnerabilities. FBHM isolates these axes, revealing that models rely on dataset-specific heuristics rather than robust reasoning, and offers a controlled environment for measuring generalization.
2605.31349.decisionReason: Meets benchmark criteria: a named, repeatable dataset with a clear scoring contract (Macro-F1) and public access via arXiv. It is a fixed benchmark usable by other teams for evaluation, not solely a viewpoint probe.

2605.31410.description: FAM-Bench evaluates multimodal language and vision-language models on Food-as-Medicine reasoning. It includes 2500 expert-verified instances across 13 health conditions, with two tasks: dish-level suitability assessment (judging if a dish is suitable for a condition) and comparative dish analysis (ranking four dishes by suitability).
2605.31410.whyItMatters: The benchmark fills a gap in food AI evaluation by testing whether models can integrate ingredient, visual, and clinical nutrition constraints to make condition-aware food decisions. It provides a standardized testbed for comparing models on grounded health-aware reasoning, which is relevant for applications in nutrition guidance and chronic disease management.
2605.31410.decisionReason: FAM-Bench defines a new evaluation object (Food-as-Medicine reasoning) with a fixed dataset and clear tasks, providing a public path via the paper and dataset availability.

2605.31251.description: ERGeoBench evaluates vision-driven embodied geo-localization in MLLMs with 2,207 globally distributed street-view panoramas under single-view, panorama-view, and embodied-view settings. It measures foundational perception, spatial awareness, common sense reasoning, and geo-localization reasoning.
2605.31251.whyItMatters: Embodied geo-localization is underexplored due to lack of fine-grained evaluation. ERGeoBench provides a unified diagnostic framework that reveals current MLLMs struggle with fine-grained perceptual operations and metric localization, supporting progress in integrated perception and spatial reasoning.
2605.31251.decisionReason: The paper presents ERGeoBench as a diagnostic benchmark with a clear evaluation object (embodied geo-localization), a fixed dataset (2,207 panoramas), defined capability dimensions and settings, and a project page with official links, providing a credible path for other teams to run or inspect it.

2605.31557.description: Egostream evaluates streaming episodic memory in egocentric vision through 2,250 curated questions across seven cognitive dimensions, expanded into 8,528 recall-conditioned evaluations using the Answer Validity Window to test recall from instant to ultra-long-term.
2605.31557.whyItMatters: Existing streaming video benchmarks lack fine-grained diagnosis of memory retention over time. Egostream provides a controlled protocol that separates genuine forgetting from world-state changes, enabling precise assessment of model memory capabilities across different temporal scales.
2605.31557.decisionReason: The benchmark offers a fixed set of curated questions and a clear scoring contract via AVW-based condition expansion, with a public project website and code link for reuse. The evaluation protocol is defined well enough for other teams to run.

2606.02246.description: Ego-METAS evaluates online temporal action segmentation in egocentric video, where models must select sensor modalities (RGB, audio, gaze, IMU, monochrome) per timestep to maximize accuracy under hardware-representative energy budgets. It includes 100+ hours of untrimmed video from multiple datasets.
2606.02246.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the gap in energy-aware perception for embodied AI by providing a standardized testbed for developing and comparing cost-aware sensor routing policies in continuous, untrimmed environments. It enables assessment of trade-offs between predictive accuracy and energy consumption, with practical implications for always-on devices.
2606.02246.decisionReason: The paper introduces a named benchmark (Ego-METAS) with a clear evaluation task, unified splits, cleaned annotations, pre-extracted features, and baseline policies, providing credible public paths for reuse and comparison.

2605.30907.description: Evaluates LLM agents on synthesis, manipulation, and comprehension tasks over financial spreadsheet workbooks, with 131 tasks and granular rubric criteria validated by expert annotators.
2605.30907.whyItMatters: Fills the gap in evaluating LLMs for spreadsheet tasks relevant to professional finance, where current models perform below 50%, providing a measure for practical deployment.
2605.30907.decisionReason: Defines a repeatable benchmark with a dataset, evaluation harness, and rubric-based scoring; public path via open-source code and dataset.

2605.30900.description: Evaluates physical reasoning in synthetic billiards environments, testing collision prediction, wall bounce reasoning, and final position estimation for multimodal LLMs.
2605.30900.whyItMatters: Addresses the gap in evaluating visual dynamics and physical reasoning capabilities of multimodal models, providing a method to assess model performance on intuitive physics tasks.
2605.30900.decisionReason: No public artifacts or official benchmark website provided; only paper link, making it unclear if there is a stable scoring contract or public reuse path.

2605.30346.description: YoCausal is a two-level benchmark that evaluates video diffusion models' understanding of temporal causality using the Violation of Expectation paradigm. It temporally reverses real-world videos as counterfactual samples and introduces two metrics: the Reverse Surprise Index (RSI) for arrow-of-time perception and the Causality Cognition Index (CCI) for disentangling genuine causal reasoning from temporal bias.
2605.30346.whyItMatters: Existing video benchmarks rely on synthetic data and do not separate temporal-direction awareness from true causal understanding. YoCausal provides a protocol that isolates causal cognition from temporal bias, enabling evaluation of whether models genuinely understand cause-and-effect relationships or only statistical patterns.
2605.30346.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear evaluation protocol, publicly available dataset and code, and a defined scoring contract via RSI and CCI metrics.

2605.30344.description: VisAnomBench is a benchmark assembled from public time-series datasets for anomaly detection, augmented with natural-language explanations selected from large vision-language models. It supports fine-tuning a parameter-efficient VLM called VisAnomReasoner for grounded anomaly detection decisions.
2605.30344.whyItMatters: Public anomaly detection benchmarks typically lack natural-language rationales, hindering fine-tuning of VLMs for interpretable decisions. VisAnomBench addresses this gap by providing labeled explanations.
2605.30344.decisionReason: No official links to code, dataset, or leaderboard are provided; evidence is insufficient to verify a public reuse path or stable scoring contract.

2605.30256.description: VideoFDB is a benchmark presented for evaluating full-duplex audio-visual conversational agents. It includes 237 dyadic clips with 11 nonverbal conversational dynamics from real-world video calls, along with a taxonomy and rubric-based LM-as-judge evaluation framework.
2605.30256.whyItMatters: Existing full-duplex benchmarks only evaluate speech, missing the audio-visual nature of natural conversation. VideoFDB aims to fill this gap by evaluating agents that must produce and interpret nonverbal cues.
2605.30256.decisionReason: The benchmark primarily supports the paper's findings and lacks a clear standalone public comparison path; no official code or dataset links are provided.

2605.30329.description: SoundnessBench evaluates LLMs' ability to judge the methodological soundness of research proposals. It contains 1,099 machine-learning research proposals reconstructed from ICLR submissions, labeled with reviewer soundness sub-scores and audited against source papers.
2605.30329.whyItMatters: Autonomous AI research agents need to evaluate research ideas before committing resources, but existing benchmarks do not test this bottleneck. SoundnessBench provides a standardized test for this capability.
2605.30329.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a clear evaluation task, publicly available data, code, and a leaderboard with standard and aggressive prompting modes.

2605.29468.description: SciIntBench is an adversarial benchmark of 810 prompts across ten responsible-conduct-of-research categories and three scientific domains. Each scenario appears in overt, covert, and benign versions to measure framing-sensitive refusal of misconduct.
2605.29468.whyItMatters: LLMs are increasingly used in scientific work, but their compliance with research integrity norms is unclear. SciIntBench aims to measure how models handle framing-sensitive ethical scenarios.
2605.29468.decisionReason: No official links to code, data, or leaderboard are provided, and the evaluation protocol is not fully specified for public use.

2605.30326.description: RoboWits is a bi-manual robotic benchmark designed to evaluate cognitive reasoning, creative tool use, and robustness to unexpected conditions. It includes 30 seed tasks and 208 mutated tasks with graded difficulty across geometry, material, and assembly-based reasoning.
2605.30326.whyItMatters: Current robotic benchmarks focus on skill-level execution, not the cognitive reasoning needed for real-world adaptation. RoboWits aims to evaluate reasoning-centric capabilities under unexpected challenges.
2605.30326.decisionReason: The benchmark primarily supports the paper's findings, and no official code or dataset links are provided, lacking a clear public reuse path.

2606.07591.description: ResearchClawBench evaluates autonomous scientific research agents across 40 tasks from 10 domains, each grounded in a published paper with provided literature and raw data. It uses expert-curated multimodal rubrics to score target-paper-level re-discovery.
2606.07591.whyItMatters: Autonomous research agents claim to accelerate science, but their end-to-end capability is unverified. ResearchClawBench provides a standardized evaluation frontier to measure progress toward reliable research re-discovery.
2606.07591.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear evaluation protocol, publicly available dataset, code, leaderboard, and ongoing submissions.

2605.29893.description: RedundancyBench is a benchmark for detecting redundant steps in agent trajectories. It contains diverse tasks with annotated trajectories where each step is labeled for its contribution to task completion.
2605.29893.whyItMatters: LLM-based agents often execute with inefficiencies, but existing evaluations focus only on task success. RedundancyBench addresses the gap in evaluating execution efficiency.
2605.29893.decisionReason: The provided link is anonymous and incomplete, with no official code or dataset available for public verification.

2605.29579.description: ReactBench evaluates multimodal large language models on cause-driven hallucination through four targeted tasks (Relational Erasure, Counterfactual Attribute, Alteration Tracing, Dense Counting) with exam-style evaluation and chain-of-thought reasoning for sub-cause identification.
2605.29579.whyItMatters: Existing hallucination benchmarks measure outcomes rather than causes. ReactBench provides a systematic testbed to diagnose specific failure modes like co-occurrence bias and fine-grained perceptual bottlenecks, offering interpretable insights for model robustness.
2605.29579.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear task definitions, evaluation format, and public project page. The benchmark defines repeatable evaluation objects and scoring contract.

2605.29653.description: PTCG-Bench evaluates LLM agents on the Pokémon Trading Card Game at two levels: single-environment decision-making and self-evolution through accumulated experience, with modular harness ablation to separate agent performance from harness design.
2605.29653.whyItMatters: Agent benchmarks often miss strategic and evolving decision-making. PTCG-Bench provides a realistic interactive environment to assess self-evolution and harness sensitivity, which are critical for deploying autonomous agents.
2605.29653.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined tasks and evaluation levels. Reusable via specified harness, though no official code/data link provided.

2605.30284.description: A framework for evaluating scientific hypothesis generation in LLMs under progressive information disclosure, comparing model hypotheses to original paper conclusions via semantic similarity.
2605.30284.whyItMatters: It assesses a model's innovativeness and grounded reasoning in scientific discovery, which is crucial for developing AI co-scientist systems.
2605.30284.decisionReason: Primarily a framework supporting one paper's findings on specific models; lacks a standalone public comparison path and stable scoring contract beyond this study.

2605.29299.description: Pocket-Dentist is an efficiency-aware benchmark for dental multimodal question answering that combines three datasets, five task types, and seven metrics to evaluate VLMs on accuracy and computational cost.
2605.29299.whyItMatters: It highlights the trade-off between model performance and efficiency for on-device dental screening, which is essential for practical deployment in resource-limited settings.
2605.29299.decisionReason: Primarily a model evaluation with a specific efficiency focus; lacks a clear public benchmark structure and reusable protocol beyond the paper's experiments.

2605.30639.description: PInVerify is an offline embodied benchmark for Active Instance Verification, where agents select viewpoints around a candidate object to decide if it matches a fine-grained description.
2605.30639.whyItMatters: It addresses the gap between navigating to an object and verifying its identity through active perception, which is crucial for embodied agents in fine-grained tasks.
2605.30639.decisionReason: The benchmark is in early preview; dataset and model weights not yet released, and code not fully tested, so public reuse path is incomplete.

2605.29833.description: OmniMatBench assesses multimodal reasoning in materials science across 19 subfields with 3,171 expert-curated QA and calculation problems, spanning four domains from fundamental knowledge to applied materials.
2605.29833.whyItMatters: Existing materials benchmarks focus on narrow tasks; OmniMatBench provides a broad reasoning benchmark revealing a substantial gap in current MLLMs, guiding AI assistant development in materials research.
2605.29833.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear dataset, tasks, and scoring. Publicly available but no direct link provided for reuse; official paper link supports publisher.

2605.29300.description: MusTBENCH evaluates temporal grounding in Large Audio-Language Models through five temporally grounded question-answering tasks, validated by music experts, to test alignment with audio regions.
2605.29300.whyItMatters: Temporal grounding is critical for music understanding, where events are localized. MusTBENCH establishes this as a missing capability and offers a challenging benchmark for improvement.
2605.29300.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined tasks and evaluation; publicly reusable, though no official data link provided.

2605.29738.description: Multi-Legal-Bench evaluates LLMs on legal reasoning across six countries, four language families, and five tasks, using structured metadata from court registries for classification and extraction.
2605.29738.whyItMatters: It enables cross-lingual and cross-jurisdictional comparison of legal reasoning, revealing that transfer quality depends more on label-set alignment than language proximity, aiding model selection in legal NLP.
2605.29738.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear tasks, data released on Hugging Face, and public evaluation protocol; projects as an ongoing comparison benchmark.

2605.29360.description: MiraBench evaluates action-conditioned reliability in robotic world models through three levels: Physics Adherence, Action-Following Fidelity, and Optimism Bias Detection, using a human-annotated corpus of over 16,000 judgments.
2605.29360.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks focus on visual fidelity, leaving unclear whether predicted futures are physically plausible, faithful to actions, and calibrated to failure. MiraBench aims to provide a diagnostic foundation for assessing world models as simulators, but its public evaluation protocol and release details are not yet specified.
2605.29360.decisionReason: No public artifact or official benchmark link is provided beyond the paper abstract; the corpus and evaluation protocol are not confirmed to be publicly available or reusable.

2605.30434.description: LongDS-Bench evaluates long-horizon, multi-turn data analysis tasks where agents must maintain, update, restore, and compose evolving analytical states. It comprises 68 tasks from real-world Kaggle notebooks spanning 2,225 turns across six domains, with an average dependency span of 11.3 turns.
2605.30434.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks focus on isolated or short interactive tasks, leaving long-horizon analytical state management untested. This benchmark reveals a critical bottleneck in agent performance, where errors concentrate in later turns and additional interaction steps do not reliably improve accuracy, aiding development of more reliable agentic systems.
2605.30434.decisionReason: The benchmark defines a repeatable evaluation object with a clear scoring contract (accuracy) and provides public code and data via GitHub. The benchmark distinguishes itself from existing tasks by focusing on long-horizon state evolution, and the release path supports external use.

2605.30058.description: HEART-Bench evaluates whether LLM agents can simulate coherent, human-like psychology. It provides 11 fictional characters with raw episodic memories, 64 decision-making scenarios based on the DIAMONDS taxonomy, and 673 multiple-choice questions with expert-annotated ground truth. Two evaluation tracks: MCQ and open-ended consciousness-narrative.
2605.30058.whyItMatters: This benchmark addresses the gap in evaluating emotional and personality consistency in LLM agents, complementing task-oriented benchmarks. It offers a standardized protocol for assessing psychological coherence, which is valuable for developing agents that can maintain stable personas and make value-consistent decisions in interactive applications.
2605.30058.decisionReason: The benchmark provides a fixed dataset and protocol with public code and data, enabling other teams to run or inspect it. It defines clear evaluation tracks and scoring, making it publicly reusable.

2605.29224.description: AgentREVEAL is a diagnostic framework that evaluates safety alignment degradation in LLM agents when web retrieval is integrated. It assesses the impact of retrieval integration and content properties on harmful compliance, using a set of harmful behaviors and retrieval sources.
2605.29224.whyItMatters: AgentREVEAL addresses the underexplored risk that safety-aligned LLMs become more compliant with harmful requests when augmented with web retrieval. Its findings highlight a safety-utility trade-off that informs the design of safer retrieval-enabled agents.
2605.29224.decisionReason: AgentREVEAL provides a repeatable evaluation object with a defined protocol for analyzing retrieval-induced safety degradation, and the associated HarmURLBench offers a public path for reuse, meeting the criteria for public_reusable.

2605.29586.description: FinVerBench evaluates financial statement verification in LLMs, using SEC 10-K XBRL filings from 43 S&P 500 companies with a four-category error taxonomy (arithmetic, cross-statement linkage, year-over-year, magnitude perturbations).
2605.29586.whyItMatters: Financial statement verification requires calibrated judgment under incomplete observability and realistic numerical rendering, not just arithmetic detection. This benchmark provides a reusable diagnostic subset to assess model performance and validity.
2605.29586.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a defined task, dataset, and protocol. It offers a public dataset and code, enabling other teams to inspect and run the evaluation. Although the scoring contract is not fully stable, the public reuse path is credible and the benchmark is designed for comparison.

2605.29427.description: The evaluation focuses on financial regulatory non-compliance detection in LLM interactions. It involves a benchmark with expert-annotated labels at query and response levels, but the exact task, environment, or scoring setup is not detailed.
2605.29427.whyItMatters: Assesses LLM compliance with financial regulations, which is critical for preventing regulatory penalties and consumer harm in financial services. The benchmark aims to measure detection capabilities across institution-specific policies.
2605.29427.decisionReason: The paper claims to release a benchmark, but no official links or artifacts are provided in the input, and the description lacks sufficient detail to confirm a repeatable evaluation object or accessible path for other teams.

2605.30637.description: EHRBench evaluates LLM-based clinical decision-making using nearly 1M QA items generated from real EHR trajectories, covering diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis tasks.
2605.30637.whyItMatters: Existing clinical decision benchmarks often lack scale and reliability; EHRBench provides a large-scale, EHR-grounded evaluation that tests models on practical inference tasks, offering insights into model capabilities and gaps for clinical deployment.
2605.30637.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear task definitions and scoring via QA accuracy; public pipeline and dataset are described, with a credible path for reuse.

2605.30090.description: DirectorBench evaluates long-form video generation across 5 dimensions (script, visual, audio, cross-modal, stability) using 80 metadata entries, 7 user profiles, and 40 checkpoint criteria.
2605.30090.whyItMatters: Current video benchmarks focus on short clips and aggregate scores, missing workflow failures and user preferences. DirectorBench provides diagnostic, profile-aware evaluation to guide improvements in long-form video generation.
2605.30090.decisionReason: Named benchmark with defined evaluation criteria and human validation; intended for model comparison, but no public code or dataset link provided, so publicReusePath is false.

2605.29446.description: CrystalXRD-Bench evaluates vision-language models on XRD peak indexing, requiring the model to identify HKL indices from rendered XRD images and CIF text across 250 samples from 10 databases.
2605.29446.whyItMatters: Existing multimodal benchmarks do not test this specialized scientific skill. CrystalXRD-Bench isolates visual extraction and crystallographic reasoning errors, providing a focused evaluation for quantitative figure understanding.
2605.29446.decisionReason: Named benchmark with fixed dataset and clear task; public availability of data and code is stated.

2605.30611.description: CraftBench evaluates scientific figure generation across three figure types and four input conditions, with human-drawn targets and a referenced VLM judge for scoring.
2605.30611.whyItMatters: Automated figure generation lacks comprehensive benchmarks covering diverse types and conditions. CraftBench provides a standardized evaluation to measure progress in editable scientific figure generation.
2605.30611.decisionReason: Named benchmark with clear protocol and public dataset on HuggingFace; code is available for reproduction.

2605.30241.description: CommunityFact evaluates misinformation detection on 15,992 claims across five languages and two domains, using accuracy against human Community Notes ratings as the scoring metric.
2605.30241.whyItMatters: Static benchmarks fail to capture dynamic, multilingual misinformation settings. CommunityFact provides a refreshable benchmark to assess model reliability in real-world verification contexts.
2605.30241.decisionReason: Named benchmark with fixed dataset and clear task; intended for model comparison, but no public data or code link is provided, so publicReusePath is false.

2605.30394.description: CodeGolf Bench evaluates concise code generation across 60 programming languages, using code golf platform problems and human performance baselines for scoring.
2605.30394.whyItMatters: Existing code benchmarks focus on correctness, not efficiency or conciseness. CodeGolf Bench offers a unique measure of LLM ability to produce minimal solutions, complementing standard code generation evaluation.
2605.30394.decisionReason: Named benchmark with a dynamic framework and live baselines; intended for model comparison, but no public code or dataset link is provided, so publicReusePath is false.

2605.29933.description: CLUBench evaluates clustering algorithms across 131 datasets (tabular, text, image) using 24 algorithms, measuring clustering performance via standard metrics like NMI, ARI, etc.
2605.29933.whyItMatters: There is no comprehensive comparison of classical, deep, and foundation-model clustering methods. CLUBench provides systematic insights into algorithm selection and performance across data types.
2605.29933.decisionReason: Named benchmark with extensive experimental setup and public protocol; availability of code and data is implied, and results are reproducible.

2605.30100.description: Chess-World-Model evaluates state tracking by predicting the exact board state after sequences of legal moves from 10 million chess games, with accuracy as the metric.
2605.30100.whyItMatters: State tracking is under-tested in realistic domains. This benchmark exposes limitations in Transformer and RNN models that scale alone may hide, offering a practical testbed for world models.
2605.30100.decisionReason: Named benchmark with fixed dataset and clear task; public availability is described, and experiments are reproducible.

2606.00123.description: CardioLens evaluates MLLMs on multi-sequence cardiac MRI interpretation, covering image understanding, report generation, and disease diagnosis using QA pairs from private hospital archives.
2606.00123.whyItMatters: The benchmark highlights the gap between public medical benchmark performance and clinical use, but its private data and lack of a public reuse path limit its value for broader model comparison.
2606.00123.decisionReason: Dataset is private and not publicly reusable; no official public benchmark artifacts or leaderboard found.

2605.30497.description: CanLegalRAGBench evaluates retrieval-augmented generation for Canadian case law with realistic queries and expert-annotated answers. It tests retrieval and answer generation grounded in legal documents.
2605.30497.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in legal RAG evaluation for Canadian law, providing realistic scenarios and revealing limitations in automatic metrics and hallucination in generated answers.
2605.30497.decisionReason: Public benchmark with clear evaluation protocol, expert annotations, and stated metrics; no official release URL provided but data appears accessible.

2605.28683.description: VeriTrip benchmarks travel planning agents on evidence-grounded reasoning over unstructured web corpora, with a verifiable knowledge base for cell-wise verification of factual reliability.
2605.28683.whyItMatters: Targets robustness of planning agents, but the benchmark's data and verification protocol are not described with public artifacts, limiting its standalone use.
2605.28683.decisionReason: No public access to the benchmark or evaluation code; authors only describe results, not a reusable benchmark.

2605.29170.description: UA-Legal-Bench is a five-task benchmark for evaluating LLMs on Ukrainian legal reasoning using court decisions, covering classification, outcome prediction, and norm extraction.
2605.29170.whyItMatters: Addresses the dearth of legal NLP benchmarks for non-English, morphologically rich languages, and provides insights into few-shot effects and model scaling in legal tasks.
2605.29170.decisionReason: Provides official dataset link with detailed metadata, evaluation code, and all model predictions, enabling reuse and comparison.

2605.29054.description: T2J-Bench benchmarks codebase conversion by transferring PyTorch code to JAX under a fixed equivalence contract with three ordered verification stages.
2605.29054.whyItMatters: Reveals that agents overestimate success on codebase conversion, but the benchmark's data and verification harness are not publicly released.
2605.29054.decisionReason: No public artifacts or release details; the benchmark is described in the paper but lacks a public reuse path.

2605.27911.description: SuiChat-CN is a Chinese group-chat benchmark for contextual suicide risk assessment, with 13,312 segments from 1,406 users.
2605.27911.whyItMatters: Pioneers risk assessment in group chats but the dataset is restricted for ethical reasons, limiting its public use.
2605.27911.decisionReason: Dataset is not publicly released; researchers must request access, so it lacks an open comparison path.

2605.28073.description: STORYLENSBENCH benchmarks preference-aligned story rewriting with structured story books and reader profiles, plus reward model and rewriting model.
2605.28073.whyItMatters: Focuses on context-aware narrative enrichment, but the benchmark is not publicly released; only the models are proposed.
2605.28073.decisionReason: No public dataset or evaluation protocol; the benchmark is introduced as part of the paper's methodology, not as a standalone public benchmark.

2605.28065.description: SpatialBench-Long evaluates AI agents on long-horizon spatial biology tasks, requiring recovery of biological claims from raw data across 24 evaluations.
2605.28065.whyItMatters: Tests agents' ability to synthesize scientific conclusions from complex spatial data, but no public data or code release is mentioned.
2605.28065.decisionReason: No official link to benchmark data or code; only the paper abstract is provided, lacking evidence of public availability.

2605.28091.description: Qwen-Image-Bench evaluates text-to-image models on five pillars including Real-world Fidelity and Creative Generation, with 1000 prompts and 56 rubric-based facets scored by a trained judge model.
2605.28091.whyItMatters: It aims to address gaps in existing T2I benchmarks by assessing application-driven capabilities for professional creative workflows, offering fine-grained diagnostics for model comparison and development.
2605.28091.decisionReason: Artifact evidence is empty; no official link to dataset, code, or leaderboard is provided, making public reuse unverifiable.

2605.28375.description: Named entity recognition dataset from PubMed abstracts on prion disease, with 317 abstracts annotated for 15 coarse and 31 fine-grained entity types, plus evaluation scripts and train/test splits.
2605.28375.whyItMatters: Fills a gap in biomedical NLP for rare diseases, enabling evaluation of fine-grained and discontinuous entity extraction under low-resource conditions.
2605.28375.decisionReason: Public dataset with clear annotation guidelines, canonical splits, and evaluation scripts; qualifies as a reusable benchmark.

2605.27887.description: PortBench evaluates LLM-driven portfolio management via a static QA dataset (6,269 questions across seven task templates) and a dynamic five-stage allocation pipeline, spanning six asset classes over ten years. Scoring includes a dual-layer correlation score and CEPS, with evaluation under three stress regimes and investor profiles.
2605.27887.whyItMatters: Existing financial benchmarks often ignore cross-asset correlations and the full portfolio management pipeline. PortBench addresses this gap by providing a comprehensive, reusable evaluation for LLM capabilities in realistic portfolio management, enabling comparison across models and informing practical deployment decisions.
2605.27887.decisionReason: PortBench is a named benchmark with a clear evaluation object (QA dataset and pipeline), a defined scoring contract (metrics and protocols), and a public code repository and dataset links, making it reusable by other teams.

2605.28241.description: PointQ-Bench is a benchmark for point cloud quality assessment, extending from scalar scoring to comprehensive quality understanding, with 3,083 point clouds and tasks like anomaly sensing, defect diagnosis, usability grading, and open-ended quality reporting.
2605.28241.whyItMatters: Current PCQA benchmarks focus on scalar prediction, leaving gaps in diagnostic and interpretable quality assessment. PointQ-Bench addresses this by evaluating models on multi-faceted quality understanding tasks, which is crucial for practical inspection scenarios where identifying defects and assessing usability is necessary.
2605.28241.decisionReason: The paper describes a benchmark with datasets and tasks, but there is no evidence of a public artifact or protocol provided, and no scoring contract description. The abstract mentions proposed tasks and protocol, but the lack of artifact evidence and official links to datasets or code makes it unclear if it is publicly reusable or available for score submission.

2605.28819.description: PEFT-Arena benchmark jointly evaluates target-domain performance and retention of pretrained capabilities for parameter-efficient finetuning methods. It covers mathematical and medical reasoning as target domains and measures general capability retention on benchmarks including BBH, IFEval, and NQ with SFT and RLVR training settings.
2605.28819.whyItMatters: Existing PEFT evaluations focus mainly on downstream accuracy, overlooking retention of pretrained abilities. This benchmark provides a stability-plasticity perspective, enabling selection of fine-tuning methods that balance task adaptation and forgetting resistance, offering a more complete assessment for practical deployment decisions.
2605.28819.decisionReason: The paper introduces a named benchmark with a clear protocol, public code, and evaluation pipelines for target and retention domains, providing a credible public path for other teams to run it.

2605.28158.description: A full-lifecycle workspace benchmark for industrial optimization agents, evaluating model construction, revision, and grounded explanation across three task modes (Build, Revise, Explain) using executable multi-file workspaces with task-specific evaluators.
2605.28158.whyItMatters: Fills the gap in benchmarking LLM agents for real industrial OR workflows, where persistent multi-artifact workspaces and multi-stage lifecycles are central, offering a more realistic evaluation of practical readiness beyond single-shot formulation tasks.
2605.28158.decisionReason: Publishable as a public reusable benchmark: it defines a repeatable evaluation object (300 workspace views from 100 topologies) with explicit scoring protocols (execution-based for Build/Revise, rubric for Explain), and provides a public GitHub repository with runnable evaluators and validation tools, enabling other teams to run or inspect it.

2605.28579.description: MUSE evaluates text-to-CAD generation of complex B-Rep assemblies via design specifications. It scores models on code validity, geometric correctness, and design-intent alignment using rubrics covering functionality, manufacturability, and assemblability. A VLM judge with human validation is used for scalable scoring.
2605.28579.whyItMatters: Existing CAD benchmarks focus on single-part geometric similarity, missing industrial requirements. MUSE provides a structured evaluation that measures practical design quality, enabling progress toward engineering-ready CAD generation.
2605.28579.decisionReason: MUSE defines a fixed benchmark with dataset, evaluation protocol, and public leaderboard, providing a comparable scoring contract and reuse path for other teams.

2605.28035.description: MTAVG-Bench 2.0 evaluates omni large language models on diagnosing high-level cinematic failures in multi-talker audio-video generation, with over 10,000 QA instances covering acting, narrative, atmosphere, and audio-visual language.
2605.28035.whyItMatters: Standard metrics like lip-sync do not capture cinematic expressiveness; this benchmark targets a gap in evaluating higher-level audio-visual quality in scene-level generation.
2605.28035.decisionReason: Primarily supports the paper's diagnostic study of failure modes; no standalone public benchmark infrastructure or comparison path is provided.

2605.28192.description: MOV-Bench contains 519 questions requiring multi-hop reasoning over temporally dispersed audio-visual evidence, evaluating omni-modal LLMs on cross-modal reasoning tasks.
2605.28192.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks offer limited investigation of multi-hop audio-visual reasoning; MOV-Bench provides a focused evaluation set for this capability.
2605.28192.decisionReason: Introduced as a benchmark but lacks public artifacts or a defined scoring protocol for external comparison; serves primarily the paper's evaluation.

2605.28161.description: MeniOmni is a multimodal benchmark for meniscus injury assessment with 746 MRI studies, supporting Stoller severity grading and diagnostic report generation, with risk-aware ordinal evaluation and semantic consistency metric.
2605.28161.whyItMatters: Addresses a gap in knee MRI benchmarks by integrating volumetric MRI data with clinical context for holistic clinical reasoning, aiming to improve safety in meniscus injury diagnosis.
2605.28161.decisionReason: Code and data are stated to be released after conference presentation; not yet publicly available, so no current reuse path.

2605.28013.description: KSAFE-MM evaluates multimodal LLM safety in Korean contexts, with 12 models tested on general and culture-specific safety risks, including jailbreak-style textual queries paired with local visual cues.
2605.28013.whyItMatters: Existing safety benchmarks are English-centric and ignore local cultural risks; KSAFE-MM provides a general-to-local pipeline for culturally grounded safety evaluation, revealing trade-offs between safety and over-refusal.
2605.28013.decisionReason: Presents a benchmark with a clear evaluation protocol and publicly available dataset for Korean multimodal safety; supports external reuse.

2605.28218.description: IFMTBench evaluates multilingual translation instruction following across seven languages, with 4,506 single-constraint and 2,838 multi-constraint items covering six constraint dimensions and five compositional patterns, scored by deterministic checkers and LLM judge.
2605.28218.whyItMatters: Addresses a gap in translation evaluation by measuring constraint adherence beyond semantic fidelity, revealing that instruction following scales with model size and general instruction rankings do not predict translation behavior.
2605.28218.decisionReason: Provides a public benchmark with a well-defined scoring protocol and available code/data on GitHub.

2605.27922.description: Harness-Bench evaluates configuration-level harness effects in agent workflows with 106 sandboxed tasks, measuring completion, process quality, efficiency, and failure behavior across model-harness pairings.
2605.27922.whyItMatters: Addresses a gap in agent evaluation by isolating harness configuration effects, showing that agent capability is configuration-level rather than model-only, and identifying execution-alignment failures.
2605.27922.decisionReason: Benchmark described only in text; no public artifacts or standardized scoring contract provided for external use.

2605.28315.description: HardMTBench is a difficulty-aware diagnostic benchmark for Chinese-English domain translation, covering 12 domains with 20,000 directional test items and annotated hardness scores based on domain knowledge, translation difficulty, and terminology load.
2605.28315.whyItMatters: Addresses the saturation of general MT benchmarks on Chinese-English by widening score separation, exposing domain-specific weaknesses in knowledge-intensive areas that quality-only metrics miss.
2605.28315.decisionReason: Provides an open-sourced dataset and code with a clear evaluation protocol, enabling external teams to run and compare on the same test set.

2605.29107.description: GEO-Bench evaluates ranking manipulation attacks in generative engine optimization under a unified protocol, measuring effectiveness and stealth across five datasets against a fixed ranker, with open-source attack implementations.
2605.29107.whyItMatters: Addresses the lack of standardized comparison in GEO attack research, enabling direct comparison across attack paradigms and supporting detection development.
2605.29107.decisionReason: Provides a standardized dataset, attack implementations, and metrics; the benchmark is designed for external reuse and comparison.

2605.28044.description: FORCEBENCH is a contrastive stress test for evidence-force calibration in cited RAG. It pairs fixed cited passages with evidence-calibrated claims and force-raised variants across five axes: relation, modality, scope, temporal validity, and numeric specificity. Evaluation is a fixed, locality-filtered set of 198 pairs.
2605.28044.whyItMatters: Current cited RAG evaluation often treats topical relevance as sufficient grounding, missing cases where a relevant source under-warrants an over-strong claim. FORCEBENCH exposes this citation laundering failure and measures evaluator calibration via monotonicity violation rate and force sensitivity.
2605.28044.decisionReason: The paper defines a named benchmark with a fixed evaluation set and explicit scoring metrics (MVR, force sensitivity). A plug-in pipeline is released for external use, though no live leaderboard is mentioned; the fixed set and clear protocol make it public_reusable.

2605.27896.description: FinBoardBench is an evaluation suite based on three financial board games: Cashflow, Acquire, and Monopoly. It assesses financial skills including personal cash flow management, corporate investment and acquisition forecasting, and competitive trade negotiations with asset auctions, using game simulations as the environment.
2605.27896.whyItMatters: Existing static financial benchmarks do not capture dynamic decision-making in complex environments. FinBoardBench provides a repeatable protocol to measure whether LLMs can translate static reasoning into successful dynamic action, addressing a gap in financial AI evaluation.
2605.27896.decisionReason: The paper presents a named benchmark with a defined task set and evaluation setup. Release artifacts or public access are not explicitly shown, but the title and abstract indicate a reusable evaluation suite with clear protocols for other teams.

2605.29074.description: Embodied3DBench is a robot-centric benchmark for low-level spatial intelligence in embodied 3D environments. It includes 6 task categories: Grounding, Spatial Relation Prediction, Multi-view Correspondence, Affordance Prediction, Grasp Point Prediction, and Trajectory Prediction, with 21k QA pairs across 12 subcategories.
2605.29074.whyItMatters: Current VLMs show strong high-level spatial reasoning but lack interaction-oriented perception. Embodied3DBench reveals this gap and provides a scalable training dataset for improvement, enabling systematic evaluation and advancement of interaction-aware multimodal systems.
2605.29074.decisionReason: The paper introduces a named benchmark with a large public QA dataset and a clear evaluation framework. It also releases a training dataset. The artifacts are described as available, indicating a public reuse path for other teams.

2605.27820.description: EgoBench is an interactive multimodal benchmark for tool-using agents. It comprises 1,045 egocentric-video-grounded tasks across four daily scenarios, with a user-agent-tool interactive environment. It assesses multimodal perception, tool invocation with multi-hop reasoning, and dynamic user interaction.
2605.27820.whyItMatters: AI agents in open environments need joint multimodal and tool-use capabilities. EgoBench provides a standardized interactive environment and deterministic joint validation to objectively measure these skills, addressing a lack of comparable benchmarks for dynamic tool-using agents.
2605.27820.decisionReason: The paper defines a named benchmark with a fixed set of tasks and a clear evaluation framework (deterministic joint validation). The task set and environment are described as available, though no explicit public link is given; the protocol is credible and reusable.

2605.27904.description: Dr-CiK is a benchmark for evaluating whether agents can retrieve forecasting-relevant supporting context from a document corpus, filter distractors, distill evidence, and generate forecasts. It provides context ablations and evaluates deep research and forecasting methods.
2605.27904.whyItMatters: Real-world forecasting requires active discovery of external context from noisy sources. Dr-CiK assesses the entire pipeline of context retrieval and use, revealing that most agents recover little evidence and are misled by distractors, guiding development of foresight-driven agents.
2605.27904.decisionReason: The paper presents a named benchmark with a defined task structure and evaluation metrics. It includes context ablations and comparisons across methods, indicating a stable protocol. Public artifacts are not explicitly shown but the benchmark is described with sufficient detail for replication.

2605.27957.description: DisasterBench is a benchmark for evaluating structured multi-agent planning over disaster-response tools. It includes 233 expert-verified tasks, 26 agents, 81 typed compatibility edges, and 5 planning paradigms. It uses First-Point-of-Failure (FPoF) for step-level failure attribution.
2605.27957.whyItMatters: Disaster response requires orchestrating heterogeneous AI tools into executable workflows. DisasterBench tests grounding under typed interface constraints, highlighting gaps between semantic reasoning and execution consistency, and providing diagnostics for failure attribution.
2605.27957.decisionReason: The paper and provided code repository clearly define the benchmark, dataset, evaluation metrics, and running instructions. The code is publicly available, providing a credible public reuse path for other teams.

2605.27805.description: ChildEval is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to infer and follow child-centered preferences in long-context conversations. It contains 29K synthesized persona profiles of children aged 3-6, with explicit and implicit preference expressions across five top-level and fourteen sub-level categories.
2605.27805.whyItMatters: Personalization for children is under-explored relative to adults. ChildEval provides a protocol to test whether LLMs can infer and follow child-specific preferences, addressing a gap in personalized conversational AI evaluation.
2605.27805.decisionReason: The paper defines a named benchmark with a public dataset and evaluation scripts available on GitHub. The dataset is released under a permissive license, and evaluation protocols are documented, making it reusable by other teams.

2605.27995.description: AsyncTool is a benchmark for evaluating asynchronous function calling in multi-task tool-use environments. It presents multiple tasks with simulated tool response latency, assessing step-level tool-call correctness, sub-task completion, and task-level end-to-end success, along with efficiency-oriented metrics.
2605.27995.whyItMatters: Real-world tool use involves delays, but existing benchmarks assume immediate responses. AsyncTool measures whether agents can coordinate multiple tasks and use idle time efficiently, identifying key failure modes for temporal reasoning and task coordination.
2605.27995.decisionReason: The paper and code repository provide a full benchmark definition, data, evaluation scripts, and setup instructions. The public GitHub repository enables other teams to run the benchmark, and the scoring contract is clear from the paper.

2605.27141.description: VitaBench 2.0 evaluates personalized and proactive agent behavior in long-term, multi-session user interactions across food delivery, in-store consumption, and online travel domains. Tasks are per-user sequences of subtasks requiring agents to infer, utilize, and update user preferences from fragmented interaction history, with an extensible memory interface for controlled comparison across memory architectures.
2605.27141.whyItMatters: Existing agent benchmarks focus on reasoning and tool use, overlooking the challenges of inferring and leveraging user preferences over time. This benchmark isolates personalization and proactivity in long-horizon tasks, providing a measurement of practical readiness for life-serving applications where models must act on implicit and evolving user needs.
2605.27141.decisionReason: Public benchmark with released code, dataset on Hugging Face, evaluation pipeline, and leaderboards, enabling model comparison and reuse by other teams.

2605.27367.description: SpatialBench is a deterministic, density-aware benchmark for spatial foundation models, spanning 19 datasets, 546 scenes, and five spatial domains. It evaluates 41 models across six paradigms on five task suites—depth, camera pose, trajectory, point-cloud reconstruction, and long-sequence streaming—under four input density settings with precomputed and pinned test frames.
2605.27367.whyItMatters: Spatial foundation models are typically evaluated only on domains they were designed for, making cross-domain generalization difficult to assess. SpatialBench provides a controlled protocol with fixed sampling and multiple density settings, enabling a holistic comparison of generalization across viewpoints, scene domains, and hardware constraints.
2605.27367.decisionReason: Public benchmark with released code, dataset archives on Hugging Face, and leaderboard, offering a reusable evaluation harness and deterministic evaluation protocol.

2605.26548.description: SEC-bench Pro measures long-horizon vulnerability discovery in software security. It includes 344 verified vulnerabilities across V8, SpiderMonkey, and Linux kernel, each paired with instructions for reproducing a working proof-of-concept. Grading uses an LLM-based judge to classify generated PoCs against vulnerable, fixed, and latest images.
2605.26548.whyItMatters: Finding real vulnerabilities requires reasoning across an entire codebase to produce a working PoC, a challenging task that is understudied. SEC-bench Pro provides a reproducible environment for evaluating long-horizon security capabilities, helping identify where models succeed and fail in realistic vulnerability hunting.
2605.26548.decisionReason: Public benchmark with released repository, Docker-based reproduction assets, leaderboards, and grading harness, enabling model evaluation and reuse by other teams.

2605.26855.description: Receipt Replay OOD is a small out-of-domain benchmark for screen replay detection. It uses receipts, which share planar geometry, curved corners, wear-and-tear artifacts, and text patterns with identity documents, to evaluate document replay detection models under cross-domain conditions without personally identifiable information constraints.
2605.26855.whyItMatters: Out-of-domain robustness of screen replay detection remains underexplored, especially under realistic domain shifts. This benchmark provides a public dataset for evaluating generalization across domains, which is critical for deployment in varied presentation attack scenarios.
2605.26855.decisionReason: Public dataset with stated availability, but no code or official evaluation protocol or leaderboard provided; still provides a reusable evaluation dataset.
